Hazel Nguyen began her music education at the age of three. Developing a controlled, prodigious technique, she has been praised for her authority over the most complex technically demanding pieces, the depth of her musical insight and charismatic stage presence. 
With a full scholarship to study at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland, she graduated with a First-Class Bachelor Degree in Joint-Principal Conducting and Piano Performance. At the Royal College of Music, she achieved Master of Music with Distinction in Piano Performance. 
Currently, Hazel is teaching at Rossall School in Lancashire and Sedbergh School in Cumbria, as well as judging competitions and performing worldwide. She is also one of the youngest examiners for ABRSM in the UK.
In addition, Hazel is a recording artist for Tomplay in Switzerland, a transcriber, an arranger and business partner for Musescore UK.
You can find her latest videos here https://www.youtube.com/user/hazel20111993/ 
In the past, Hazel was awarded Worthing Pianist of The Year. At Brighton Springboard Music Festival, she won the Senior Championship, as well as the Senior Concerto Class. As a result, she will be performing with Brighton Orchestra in the next seasons. 
Her virtuosic recording of Beethoven’s Bagatelle op.33 no.5 was played on BBC Radio 3 and made signature for their program In Tune. In Glasgow, producing the best performance of a Mozart Concerto, she was awarded Jock Holden Memorial Trophy. Hazel won the Rosanne Archibald prize for the most promising musician at Blackburn Music Festival and was also a winner at Glasgow Rising Star competition. 
------------------------
Nghệ sĩ piano Hazel Nguyen, tên đầy đủ là Nguyễn Ngọc Trà My, bắt đầu học nhạc từ năm ba tuổi. Kỹ thuật trên phím đàn của cô được cho là xuất sắc. Hazel thường được khen ngợi vì chinh phục thành công những tác phẩm đòi hỏi kỹ thuật phức tạp nhất, chiều sâu âm nhạc sâu lắng nhất, và trên hết là những màn biểu diễn lôi cuốn của cô. 
Với học bổng toàn phần trao tặng bởi Học Viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Scotland năm 2012, cô đã tốt nghiệp chuyên ngành Piano và Chỉ Huy Dàn Nhạc với tấm bằng hạng nhất. Ngay sau đó, Hazel đã tốt nghiệp thạc sĩ chuyên ngành biểu diễn Piano tại Học viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Anh. 
Hiện tại, Hazel đang giảng dạy tại trường Rossall thuộc hạt Lancashire và trường Sedbergh tại hạt Cumbria, Anh Quốc. Cô cũng tham gia các hoạt động biểu diễn và làm giám khảo cho các cuộc thi âm nhạc trong nước và quốc tế. Thêm vào đó, Hazel là một trong những thành viên trẻ nhất của hội đồng chấm thi âm nhạc hoàng gia Anh ABRSM.
Gần đây, cô là nghệ sĩ thu âm cho hãng Tomplay của Thụy Sĩ, và cũng là  một nhà soạn nhạc và phát triển cho ứng dụng Musescore ở Anh.
Bạn có thể tìm thấy những video của Hazel tại https://www.youtube.com/user/hazel20111993/ 
Những năm qua, Hazel được trao giải Nghệ sĩ piano danh giá của năm tại Worthing. Tại Liên hoan âm nhạc Brighton Springboard, cô đã giành giải nhất tại 3 hạng mục khác nhau, cũng như giải nhất cuộc thi Concerto. Cô sẽ biểu diễn cùng Dàn nhạc Brighton trong các mùa diễn tiếp theo.

Cô cũng là người chiến thắng tại cuộc thi Ngôi sao đang lên của Glasgow. Hazel còn giành giải thưởng Rosanne Archibald cho nghệ sĩ triển vọng nhất tại Blackburn Music Festival.

Bloch E.Pastorale No 7 from Enfantines.YT_description: Pastorale is the sort of melody that I can imagine a young child singing to themselves as they play.  I've been discussing ideas concerning pedaling in some of the earlier selections, so it's worth noting that Pastorale is fairly easy to bring off without any pedal, as long as fingerings are carefully followed, especially the finger substitution in m. 20.  Pick up the tempo starting in m. 29, as the tension builds. Be careful not to rush the last page, as the false recapitulations tease the listener.  If you're patient, the return of the true original theme will be all the more satisfying.

Prelude No.3, second extract from the forthcoming album “Préludes Avant le Jeu” composed of 16 Préludes and 8 Interludes
Piecing them together, I saw they constituted a whole, not unlike when puzzle pieces, fitted together, reveal the image on the box, though here the image I gleaned was a portrait of childhood, both past and in the process of becoming. 
I chose to record on my upright piano so that it would leave its mark on the music; I wanted its asperities and imperfections incorporated into the sound of the pieces. 
The project ended during confinement and I will release several extracts from the album before its next release. Be Well.

Performed Live on April 16th 2012 by pianist Sebastian Stanley. See http://www.sebastianstanley.com for more clips, reviews, concert dates and more.

Sebastian Stanley, the young and critically acclaimed British pianist has given recitals in all reaches of the globe. Since graduating from the Royal College of Music 4 years ago his career has gone from strength to strength with his performances receiving rave reviews. He has been described as 'a rare talent', 'Destined for the greatest concert halls' having 'exquisitely sensitive playing' and showing 'astounding virtuosity' by the critics. He has also performed in over 100 venues around the UK as a soloist for festivals, music clubs and concert societies. His expansive solo and concerto repertoire ranges from works by Scarlatti and Bach to Tchaikovsky, Liszt, Busoni and Da Falla; over 50 composers in total.

Sebastian was a late starter; having had his first piano lesson aged 13. After the astonishing progress made in the first two years he went onto the RCM aged 15 where he had the help of Emily Jeffrey, Niel Immelman, Kathron Sturrock and Ruth Nye. Most recently the world-renowned teacher and competition adjudicator Christopher Elton has become his mentor. He has also received master class tuition from piano legends such as Menahem Pressler, Claude Frank, Gary Graffman, Olga Kern, John Lill, Joanna MacGreggor and Stephen Kovacevich.

Winner of several international prizes including the coveted Chappell Medal at the RCM (Top award at the conservatoire for piano playing) and 1st Prize in the International Hindemith competition in Germany, Sebastian is making an impact on the competition circuit. He has broadcast on BBC Radio 3's In tune and Breakfast shows, Celtic Music Radio, and has been signed by the label EMEC Discos for a 4 year period after showing particular talents for the Spanish classical genre. His first disc 'El amor y la muerte' has just been released to critical acclaim and he will be recording a double disc set of music by Granados later this year.

Sign the petition to save the Arctic on: https://www.savethearctic.org
Visit Greenpeace here: http://www.greenpeace.org/
'Elegy for the Arctic' is available everywhere now: https://einaudi.lnk.to/ElegyForTheArcticID

Ludovico Einaudi performs an original piece "Elegy for the Arctic", on the Arctic Ocean to call for its protection, on June 17th, 2016

With a grand piano on a floating platform in front of a glacier, Einaudi played an original piece composed for the cause

The acclaimed composer has turned into music the voices of the eight million people that asks for Arctic protection

With this action, Greenpeace is urging the OSPAR Commission not to miss the opportunity to protect international Arctic waters under its mandate at this week's meeting in Tenerife

Through his music, acclaimed Italian composer and pianist Ludovico Einaudi has added his voice to those of eight million people from across the world demanding protection for the Arctic. 
Einaudi performed one of his own compositions on a floating platform in the middle of the Ocean, against the backdrop of the Wahlenbergbreen glacier (in Svalbard, Norway). 
Travelling on board Greenpeace ship Arctic Sunrise on the eve of a significant event for the future of the Arctic: this week's meeting of the OSPAR Commission, which could secure the first protected area in Arctic international waters.

Bloch E.Melody No 6 from Enfantines.YT_description: Melody serves as the emotional core of the Enfantines collection.  Although there's only one pedal marking, I've chosen to use judicious pedal throughout to maintain a cohesive mood.  There's an implied pedal in m. 10, which means that you have to use the pedal if you're going to achieve what's written in the score, pedal marking or not. Also, Bloch has indicated continuous pedal starting in m. 42 for the final six measures.  So, using pedal will achieve a unified whole, but be careful not to blur the harmonic changes.  Bloch's beautiful harmonies should be kept clear and distinct.

Ellmenreich A.Tiefes Leid und Trost (Dee.YT_description:
Albert Ellmenreich: Musikalische Genrebilder, Sammlung leichter Charakterstücke Op.14 - No.2 (& No.3?) Tiefes Leid und Trost

Albert Ellmenreich (1816-1905) was a German composer and actor born in Karlsruhe. He composed operas and songs, while he is known only for an easy piano piece titled "Spinnliedchen (Spinning Song)" today.

According to Hofmeister Monatsberichte, the first edition of Ellmenreich's "Musikalische Genrebilder Op.14" published by Hofmeister consists of seven pieces including famous "Spinnliedchen", but the Schirmer's edition consists of six pieces: the second piece "Tiefes Leid" and the third piece "Trost" were probably combined into one piece titled "Tiefes Leid und Trost (Sorrow and Consolation)".

Bortkiewicz S.The Hardy Tin Soldier No 3.PS_title: The Hardy Tin Soldier No 3 from Andersens Fairy Tales Op 30
Bortkiewicz S.The Hardy Tin Soldier No 3.YT_description:
"The Hardy Tin Soldier" is the 3rd of 12 pieces from the suite "Aus Andersens Marchen", Op. 30, subtitled "A Musical Picture Book" by the Russian/Ukranian composer Serge Bortkiewicz.  Each piece in the suite is based in some way on a fairy tale written by Hans Christian Andersen.  This third piece takes the form of a march with requisite bugle calls telling the tale of the one-legged tin soldier who falls in love with a toy ballerina before he accidentally falls into the stove and melts.  

I found this lovely suite about 12 years ago while rummaging through some old sheet music at a music store in Munich.  Although my copy is yellowed and aged, I am pleased to say this suite is still in print.  The pieces in it are all lovely in their own way, and are fun to play.  Hopefully my humble recordings will inspire others to explore this unjustly neglected music.     

The 12 movements are:

  1.  Die Prinzessin auf dr Erbse (The Princess and the Pea)
  2.  Die Glocke (The Bell)
  3.  Der standhafte Zinnsoldat (The Hardy Tin Soldier)
  4.  Der Engel (The Angel)
  5.  Die Blumen der kelinen Ida (Little Ida's Flowers)
  6.  Die Nachtigall (The Nightingale)
  7.  Es ist ganz gewiss (It is Quite Certian)
  8.  Das Kind im Grabe (The Child in the Grave)
  9.  Der Schmetterling (The Butterfly)
10.  Das hassliche junge Entelein (The Ugly Duckling)
11.  Goldschatz (The Golden Treasure)
12.  Das eherne Schwein (The Metal Pig)

Chapple B.Come Dancing.YT_description:
Brian Chapple provides a few introductory notes on the pieces in 'On the Cool Side' and says of this, the eighth piece:

'"Come Dancing" should be an affectionate parody of a tango (and the BBC Television programme)'. 

Who remembers 'Come Dancing'? (Other than me and Brian Chapple, that is.) It was a poor man's forerunner of 'Strictly Come Dancing' without the celebrities or razzamatazz. The dancers all behaved impeccably and you could identify them by the numbers they had pinned to their clothes (well, that's my memory, anyway). It was broadcast in black and white as colour television had not yet been invented and for young children it was the most boring thing in the world to watch. Even worse than snooker (try enjoying that without colour!)

Burgmuller J.F.Rondo alla turca Op 68.YT_description:
From "La Corbeille de Roses (Basket of roses) - 4 Morceaux brillantes & faciles"
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The German composer (Johann) Friedrich Burgmüller (1806-74) trained in his own country but moved to France in 1832, and settled there, becoming a French citizen. He was a successful piano teacher and composer of salon pieces and studies.   Although the other pieces in this set (clearly aimed at young ladies' drawing rooms) are forgotten, this one remains popular - and I am by no means the first to put it on YouTube (I particularly like the 2009 video by a young lad called Evan, who puts the piece over with a 'joie de vivre' that I would find hard to copy!).  I put my performance here to invite comparison with the Turkish rondo by Steibelt, which I uploaded in September 2012.  Incidentally, this is not a difficult piece except for some rapid chord leaps, and also the registration problem with some pianos (including mine) of projected the melody in the weaker upper register over the repeated chords in the middle register.  My thumbnail shows a details from a (colourized) illustration of  musicians in Ottoman Aleppo (mid-18th century).

Kabalevsky D.A dramatic event No 30 from.PS_title: A dramatic event No 30 from 30 pieces for children Op 27
Kabalevsky D.A dramatic event No 30 from.YT_description:
Kabalevsky, Op. 27, no. 30 Dramatic Event
Well, it's a wrap!  Thirty pieces in 31 days.  Kabalevsky ends his Op. 27 with this exciting and emotional piece.  The dotted rhythm adds greatly to the overall drama, as does the amazing crescendo that begins at pianissimo in m. 27 and culminates in a powerful fortissimo on a beautiful D flat major chord in m. 48.  Be careful not to get too loud too soon!  Note that Kabalevsky writes in his own ritardando towards the end by simply elongating the note values (m. 66-70).  A terrific piece to round out a great collection of music!

INFO:
Vorliegendes Werk "Im Grünen" op.99 -- Zehn Kinderstücke für Klavier des russischen Komponisten Alexander Gretchaninov (1864-1956) ist eine Sammlung von insgesamt 10 relativ kurzen Charakterstücken, die neben der hier betreffenden Version 'Klavier zu zwei Händen' auch als Version 'Klavier zu vier Händen' existiert.
Es handelt sich um sehr fantasievoll ausgestaltete Klavier-Miniaturen, die charakterlich und atmosphärisch an romantische Vorbilder anknüpfen möchten. Da gibt es beispielsweise die 'Ballade' (Nr. 3), 'Im Walde verirrt' (Nr. 4), oder aber 'Auf dem Lande' (Nr. 8), alles kurze Impressionen, die sich mit einem sehnsuchtsvollen Blick in eine ländlich-idyllisch inspirierte Gedankenwelt wenden.
Gretschaninoffs 'Im Grünen' ist eine sinnvolle Ergänzung zum herkömmlichen Klavierunterricht ab der unteren Mittelstufe. 

From this often-neglected Russian master come these ten beautiful
studies inspired by nature. They are all highly accessible and
suitable for 2nd-3rd year students and above.

Groundbreaking composer and pianist Ludovico Einaudi – whose unique musical style is renowned around the world – returns with a new album ‘Elements’. Recorded at Einaudi’s Italian home, ‘Elements’ features 12 tracks, which interweave piano, strings, percussion, guitar and electronica and it is simultaneously exhilarating and transcendent. It is inspired by nature’s elements, mathematical and scientific elements, musical forms and works of art.

Says Einaudi: “I saw new frontiers – on the edge between what I knew and what I didn’t know – that I had long wanted to explore: creation myths, the periodic table, Euclid's geometry, Kandinsky’s writings, the matter of sound, and of colour, the stems of wild grass in a meadow, the shapes of the landscape. For months I wandered in a seemingly chaotic mix of images, thoughts and feelings. Then, gradually, everything came together in a dance, as if all the elements were parts of the same world, and myself within it.”

Burgmuller J.F.The Gypsies Op 109 No 4.YT_description:
Friedrich Burgmüller -  Les bohémiens op.109 n 4
Fausto Bongelli, piano
Friedrich Burgmüller, in Paris known under the French form of his name, Frédéric, was born in Regensburg in 1806, the son of the composer, pianist and music teacher Johann August Franz Burgmüller, and elder brother of the composer, conductor and pianist Norbert Burgmüller. Friedrich Burgmüller was taught by his father. After the latter’s death in 1824 he followed him as director of music in Düsseldorf, teaching music in Mühlhausen and as a cellist in Basel. In 1832 he settled in Paris, where he won a considerable reputation as a piano teacher, and internationally as a composer of salon pieces and studies. He did much to promote the work of his brother Norbert, four years his junior, whose career had been cut short by his sudden death at the spa in Aachen in 1836. Friedrich Burgmüller’s activities brought continued success in Paris. Many of his compositions proved successful among amateurs, for whom his pieces offered limited technical challenges, coupled with the satisfaction of musical interest. His Études (‘Studies’) have continued to provide a basis for piano teaching and the development of technical proficiency.

Czerny C.Easy exercises Op 139 No 42.YT_description:
こんにちは！

今日は、一気に70曲、ツェルニー100番の残りを載せます！！（撮影と編集、た、た、大変だった…）
通知がとんでもないことになってしまいますが、今日だけご容赦いただけたら幸いです。
たくさんの方からずっとリクエストいただいていたにも関わらず、遅くなってしまいました…！
この動画が少しでも皆様の練習のお役に立てたら嬉しいです😄


⭐ツェルニー100番について

ツェルニー100番においてはほぼペダルは使わず、指でのレガートを意識しています。
それは小さい頃から必ず意識したほうが良いことです。
この練習曲集において、速く適当に弾いてしまうことは何よりも危険です。とにかくゆっくり丁寧に、自分の音を聞きながら弾くことを絶対に推奨します（我が生徒たちにも口酸っぱく言っていることです）

私自身、今回演奏する際に何よりも重視したのは丁寧さです。実は速く弾くことよりもゆっくり弾くことのほうが難しかったりします。ぜひ皆様も、ゆっくり丁寧に自分の音を聞きながら練習してみてくださいね😉🎵

ーーーー

小さい頃から大好きだったツェルニー。
今では教える立場となり、「教えるために弾く」場面が増え、その魅力を再認識する日々を送っていました。
嫌いな方も多いツェルニーですが、私は先生の演奏やピアニストのCDに憧れ、こんな風に弾けるようになりたい…！と、一生懸命に練習していた気がします。今の時代非常に便利な動画でツェルニーを見て、楽しく練習してもらえたら。ツェルニーのことを大好きになってもらえたら。そんな気持ちを込めて、演奏いたしました。

手首や指の使い方が一番伝わりやすいアングルで撮ったつもりでおります。音だけでなく、フィジカルな面での使い方も是非、参考にしていただければ嬉しいです。

Florence Price (1887-1953) was an African-American classical composer, pianist, organist and music teacher.  Many of her works are awaiting rediscovery.

Kabalevsky Op. 27 no. 16 Lyrical Piece
I've heard this piece played with great drama and a heavy pedal.  If one follows the score, it's clear that the dynamics are actually quite understated and the role of the pedal is very specific; to allow the low quarter notes to extend to the next set of eighth notes.  I'm using a half pedal to get a bell or chime effect.  There's an undercurrent of menace with that beautiful, spiraling melody underscored by the rhythmically insistent left hand.  Wouldn't this make a great theme for a murder mystery?  I really like the way the ground falls away beneath your feet in measure 17, as the key changes.

こんにちは！

今日は、一気に70曲、ツェルニー100番の残りを載せます！！（撮影と編集、た、た、大変だった…）
通知がとんでもないことになってしまいますが、今日だけご容赦いただけたら幸いです。
たくさんの方からずっとリクエストいただいていたにも関わらず、遅くなってしまいました…！
この動画が少しでも皆様の練習のお役に立てたら嬉しいです😄


⭐ツェルニー100番について

ツェルニー100番においてはほぼペダルは使わず、指でのレガートを意識しています。
それは小さい頃から必ず意識したほうが良いことです。
この練習曲集において、速く適当に弾いてしまうことは何よりも危険です。とにかくゆっくり丁寧に、自分の音を聞きながら弾くことを絶対に推奨します（我が生徒たちにも口酸っぱく言っていることです）

私自身、今回演奏する際に何よりも重視したのは丁寧さです。実は速く弾くことよりもゆっくり弾くことのほうが難しかったりします。ぜひ皆様も、ゆっくり丁寧に自分の音を聞きながら練習してみてくださいね😉🎵

ーーーー

小さい頃から大好きだったツェルニー。
今では教える立場となり、「教えるために弾く」場面が増え、その魅力を再認識する日々を送っていました。
嫌いな方も多いツェルニーですが、私は先生の演奏やピアニストのCDに憧れ、こんな風に弾けるようになりたい…！と、一生懸命に練習していた気がします。今の時代非常に便利な動画でツェルニーを見て、楽しく練習してもらえたら。ツェルニーのことを大好きになってもらえたら。そんな気持ちを込めて、演奏いたしました。

手首や指の使い方が一番伝わりやすいアングルで撮ったつもりでおります。音だけでなく、フィジカルな面での使い方も是非、参考にしていただければ嬉しいです。



 このチャンネルでは、主にピアノ学習中に必ず通るエチュードやバッハを載せています🌸

------------------------
Hazel Nguyen began her music education at the age of three. Developing a controlled, prodigious technique, she has been praised for her authority over the most complex technically demanding pieces, the depth of her musical insight and charismatic stage presence. 
With a full scholarship to study at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland, she graduated with a First-Class Bachelor Degree in Joint-Principal Conducting and Piano Performance. At the Royal College of Music, she achieved Master of Music with Distinction in Piano Performance. 
Currently, Hazel is teaching at Rossall School in Lancashire and Sedbergh School in Cumbria, as well as judging competitions and performing worldwide. She is also one of the youngest examiners for ABRSM in the UK.
In addition, Hazel is a recording artist for Tomplay in Switzerland, a transcriber, an arranger and business partner for Musescore UK.
You can find her latest videos here https://www.youtube.com/user/hazel20111993/ 
In the past, Hazel was awarded Worthing Pianist of The Year. At Brighton Springboard Music Festival, she won the Senior Championship, as well as the Senior Concerto Class. As a result, she will be performing with Brighton Orchestra in the next seasons. 
Her virtuosic recording of Beethoven’s Bagatelle op.33 no.5 was played on BBC Radio 3 and made signature for their program In Tune. In Glasgow, producing the best performance of a Mozart Concerto, she was awarded Jock Holden Memorial Trophy. Hazel won the Rosanne Archibald prize for the most promising musician at Blackburn Music Festival and was also a winner at Glasgow Rising Star competition. 
------------------------
Nghệ sĩ piano Hazel Nguyen, tên đầy đủ là Nguyễn Ngọc Trà My, bắt đầu học nhạc từ năm ba tuổi. Kỹ thuật trên phím đàn của cô được cho là xuất sắc. Hazel thường được khen ngợi vì chinh phục thành công những tác phẩm đòi hỏi kỹ thuật phức tạp nhất, chiều sâu âm nhạc sâu lắng nhất, và trên hết là những màn biểu diễn lôi cuốn của cô. 
Với học bổng toàn phần trao tặng bởi Học Viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Scotland năm 2012, cô đã tốt nghiệp chuyên ngành Piano và Chỉ Huy Dàn Nhạc với tấm bằng hạng nhất. Ngay sau đó, Hazel đã tốt nghiệp thạc sĩ chuyên ngành biểu diễn Piano tại Học viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Anh. 
Hiện tại, Hazel đang giảng dạy tại trường Rossall thuộc hạt Lancashire và trường Sedbergh tại hạt Cumbria, Anh Quốc. Cô cũng tham gia các hoạt động biểu diễn và làm giám khảo cho các cuộc thi âm nhạc trong nước và quốc tế. Thêm vào đó, Hazel là một trong những thành viên trẻ nhất của hội đồng chấm thi âm nhạc hoàng gia Anh ABRSM.
Gần đây, cô là nghệ sĩ thu âm cho hãng Tomplay của Thụy Sĩ, và cũng là  một nhà soạn nhạc và phát triển cho ứng dụng Musescore ở Anh.
Bạn có thể tìm thấy những video của Hazel tại https://www.youtube.com/user/hazel20111993/ 
Những năm qua, Hazel được trao giải Nghệ sĩ piano danh giá của năm tại Worthing. Tại Liên hoan âm nhạc Brighton Springboard, cô đã giành giải nhất tại 3 hạng mục khác nhau, cũng như giải nhất cuộc thi Concerto. Cô sẽ biểu diễn cùng Dàn nhạc Brighton trong các mùa diễn tiếp theo. 
Bản thu âm Beethoven Bagatelle op.33/5 của cô đã phát trên BBC Radio 3 và được dùng làm nhạc nền chính cho chương trình In Tune của họ. Tại Glasgow, nhờ màn trình diễn thuyết phục của Mozart Concerto số 12 cung La trưởng, Hazel đã chiến thắng với Cúp tưởng niệm Jock Holden dành cho người chơi Mozart xuất sắc nhất. Cô cũng là người chiến thắng tại cuộc thi Ngôi sao đang lên của Glasgow. Hazel còn giành giải thưởng Rosanne Archibald cho nghệ sĩ triển vọng nhất tại Blackburn Music Festival.

Kullak T.Witches Dance Op 4 No 2.YT_description:
With this piece (played at a viewer's request) I am marking the centenary of the death of Ernst Kullak (1855-1914), a German pianist and composer.  He was the nephew of the far more famous Theodor Kullak, at whose music academy he studied.  This short piece comes from a set of six 'tone pieces' published in 1885, but at some stage in the 20th century it seems to have been anthologized and misattributed to his uncle.  It is widely learned both in the original piano version and a clarinet arrangement, and has been on  ABRSM Grade 3 syllabuses for both instruments.  Thus, what is probably the most-played piece attributed to Theodor Kullak seems to be not by him at all!

My thumbnail shows a detail from an early 18th century woodcut of a circle of witches dancing around a central figure.  From Wellcome Images (source and licence details: https://tinyurl.com/yyakwv8z ).

Easton M.In a reflective mood (No 1 from.YT_description:
Michael Easton was born in Hertfordshire, England, in 1954. He was encouraged to pursue music by a local composer, Elizabeth Poston, and eventually entered the Royal Academy of Music where the help and encouragement of Sir Lennox Berkeley confirmed his ambition to be a composer. On leaving the Royal Academy he was employed in the music publishing world, first with J & W Chester and then with Novello & Company. As an ambassador for their publications he was required to travel widely in Europe, America and the Far East. This brought him to Australia where, in 1982, he was head-hunted by Allans Music and decided to make Melbourne his home.

Once in Australia he quickly established himself as a practical and inventive composer able to respond to commissions of all kinds, as a brilliant arranger of other people's music, and as an all-round musician of wide abilities. By 1986 he felt able to retire from the music publishing world and devote himself entirely to work .

His famous collection called MOODs for piano (1981) was written whilst Easton was staying at his sisters home near Winchester England. 

"it is a particuarly nice house with a splendid garden and i remember the music was written under a large tree that shaded me from the sun and the rain."

(2004). Michael Easton : Represented Artist Profile : Australian Music Centre. [online] Available at: https://www.australianmusiccentre.com.au/artist/easton-michael [Accessed 20 Dec. 2019].

Kabalevsky D.A tale Op 27 No 22.YT_description:
Kabalevsky Op. 27 no. 22 A Tale
Shirley calls this piece 'the Cirque du Soleil one', which I think makes a lot of sense.  Both share a mysterious, dream-like quality. If you're wondering what I'm doing at the very end - I wasn't happy with the volume of the ppp low F sharp, so I started experimenting and came up with something new.  I'm pressing the key down most of the way with my left hand, and then playing it with my right hand, which results in a very quiet note if done correctly.  I got a kick out of my 'getting psyched' moment at the beginning, so I left it in.

Chaminade C.Intermezzo Op 123 No 2.YT_description:
Cécile Chaminade (1857-1944) was a popular, highly skilled, and prolific French composer and pianist. Her Album des Enfants, Op. 123 (1906) is a delightful collection of character pieces and dances that can serve as excellent pedagogical material for the developing pianist. 

Her music reminds piano students that great art emerges from the human spirit, developed by hard work--irrespective of gender or nationality. Since Chaminade is under-appreciated today, these recordings of her pieces hope to raise awareness of her contributions to the trajectory of Western Art music--especially in the realm of piano pedagogy. Fellow composer Ambroise Thomas complimented the strength of Chaminade’s work: "This is not a woman who composes, but a composer who is a woman." This piece was performed by Chicago-area pianist and teacher, Faith Loewe Lucas, in February, 2020.

Production credits: David Huettner and Anna Friedman. Location: St. John Lutheran Church, Forest Park, IL.

Heller S.Op 45 No 10 in D minor - Vesper.YT_description:
Phillip Sear plays a short study in D minor - sometimes called 'Vesper Song' - from a set of 25 studies from around 1845 by Stephen Heller.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Since recording some other studies a few years ago, I have rather neglected the music of the Hungarian pianist and composer Stephen Heller (Heller István (1813 -- 88)) - mainly owing the unfeasibly large hands needed to perform many of his works correctly.  The English titles appear in American and British editions, and are still used today - but I am not sure if they are authentic, as they do not appear in early European editions.   Heller produces a fine piece of music using figurations usually found in finger-strengthening exercises.

こんにちは！

今日は、一気に70曲、ツェルニー100番の残りを載せます！！（撮影と編集、た、た、大変だった…）
通知がとんでもないことになってしまいますが、今日だけご容赦いただけたら幸いです。
たくさんの方からずっとリクエストいただいていたにも関わらず、遅くなってしまいました…！
この動画が少しでも皆様の練習のお役に立てたら嬉しいです😄


⭐ツェルニー100番について

ツェルニー100番においてはほぼペダルは使わず、指でのレガートを意識しています。
それは小さい頃から必ず意識したほうが良いことです。
この練習曲集において、速く適当に弾いてしまうことは何よりも危険です。とにかくゆっくり丁寧に、自分の音を聞きながら弾くことを絶対に推奨します（我が生徒たちにも口酸っぱく言っていることです）

私自身、今回演奏する際に何よりも重視したのは丁寧さです。実は速く弾くことよりもゆっくり弾くことのほうが難しかったりします。ぜひ皆様も、ゆっくり丁寧に自分の音を聞きながら練習してみてくださいね😉🎵

ーーーー

小さい頃から大好きだったツェルニー。
今では教える立場となり、「教えるために弾く」場面が増え、その魅力を再認識する日々を送っていました。
嫌いな方も多いツェルニーですが、私は先生の演奏やピアニストのCDに憧れ、こんな風に弾けるようになりたい…！と、一生懸命に練習していた気がします。今の時代非常に便利な動画でツェルニーを見て、楽しく練習してもらえたら。ツェルニーのことを大好きになってもらえたら。そんな気持ちを込めて、演奏いたしました。

手首や指の使い方が一番伝わりやすいアングルで撮ったつもりでおります。音だけでなく、フィジカルな面での使い方も是非、参考にしていただければ嬉しいです。


＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝

このチャンネルでは、主にピアノ学習中に必ず通るエチュードやバッハを載せています🌸

Czerny C.Easy exercises Op 139 No 90.YT_description:
こんにちは！

今日は、一気に70曲、ツェルニー100番の残りを載せます！！（撮影と編集、た、た、大変だった…）
通知がとんでもないことになってしまいますが、今日だけご容赦いただけたら幸いです。
たくさんの方からずっとリクエストいただいていたにも関わらず、遅くなってしまいました…！
この動画が少しでも皆様の練習のお役に立てたら嬉しいです😄


⭐ツェルニー100番について

ツェルニー100番においてはほぼペダルは使わず、指でのレガートを意識しています。
それは小さい頃から必ず意識したほうが良いことです。
この練習曲集において、速く適当に弾いてしまうことは何よりも危険です。とにかくゆっくり丁寧に、自分の音を聞きながら弾くことを絶対に推奨します（我が生徒たちにも口酸っぱく言っていることです）

私自身、今回演奏する際に何よりも重視したのは丁寧さです。実は速く弾くことよりもゆっくり弾くことのほうが難しかったりします。ぜひ皆様も、ゆっくり丁寧に自分の音を聞きながら練習してみてくださいね😉🎵

ーーーー

小さい頃から大好きだったツェルニー。
今では教える立場となり、「教えるために弾く」場面が増え、その魅力を再認識する日々を送っていました。
嫌いな方も多いツェルニーですが、私は先生の演奏やピアニストのCDに憧れ、こんな風に弾けるようになりたい…！と、一生懸命に練習していた気がします。今の時代非常に便利な動画でツェルニーを見て、楽しく練習してもらえたら。ツェルニーのことを大好きになってもらえたら。そんな気持ちを込めて、演奏いたしました。

手首や指の使い方が一番伝わりやすいアングルで撮ったつもりでおります。音だけでなく、フィジカルな面での使い方も是非、参考にしていただければ嬉しいです。


＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝

このチャンネルでは、主にピアノ学習中に必ず通るエチュードやバッハを載せています🌸

Kabalevsky D.Scherzo Op 27 No 14.YT_description:
Kabalevsky Op. 27 no. 14 Scherzo
This Scherzo includes a number of important techniques, including staccato articulation, chromatic fingerings and hand crossing.  Bring out the rhythmic figure of dotted quarter note, followed by three eighth notes, which is an important unifying device. I find this piece a great example of how Kabalevsky was able to create completely unique soundscapes within these miniatures.

Heller S.Op 45 No 23 Allegro di molto in.YT_description:
Phillip Sear plays a short study in D minor - sometimes called 'Through Wind and Rain' - from a set of 25 studies from around 1845 by Stephen Heller.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Since recording some other studies a few years ago, I have rather neglected the music of the Hungarian pianist and composer Stephen Heller (Heller István (1813 -- 88)) - mainly owing the unfeasibly large hands needed to perform many of his works correctly.  The English titles appear in American and British editions, and are still used today - but I am not sure if they are authentic, as they do not appear in early European editions.

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 132 C major.YT_description:
Margherita Torretta plays Scarlatti Sonata K.132 in C major.  Recorded in Lugano (Switzerland),on December 2016. Steinway concert grand, model D

Domenico scarlatti(1685– 1757) was an Italian composer who spent much of his life in the service of the Portuguese and Spanish royal families. He is classified primarily as a Baroque composer chronologically, although his music was influential in the development of the Classical Style and he was one of the few Baroque composers to transition into the classical period. He composed in a variety of musical forms, although today he is known mainly for his 555 keyboard sonatas. The keyboard sonata K.132 “Cantabile” has a single movement in a binary form with suggestive dissonance and figurations, harmonic audacity in its use of discords, and also unconventional modulations  to remote keys.

At Miss Florence's

Part of the cycle 'Scenes of Childhood', piano pieces commissioned by Clare Drummond in May 2012 and inspired by her recollections of a Cumbrian childhood. (http://youtu.be/4u_5h59H2Mo)


At Miss Florence’s

Miss Florence was our first schoolteacher when we were very young.
She ran a very small school, which even then was rather extraordinarily old-fashioned – for example we wrote on slates with slate pencils. She was an excellent teacher but extremely strict and would box our ears if we dropped our slates, especially if they broke.
The school was in the shadow of a huge cotton mill, and we would see the employees going to work in pinafores with their hair in turbans to keep it out of the machinery. They were referred to as “the mill girls” and we were absolutely forbidden by Miss Florence to have anything to do with them. All of the children adopted a rather curious sing-song voice when talking to her, mostly a monotone, but flipping slightly up and then down in the middle and then back to the original tone.

Hi all, today the famous song "I Will Wait for You" by M.Legrand.  I listened also to a version of the same composer M.Legrand that plays it in many keys. This  my version I played in four different keys, increasing each repetition of a semitone (Dm, D # m, Em.Fm) In any case, I tried to play it the simplest possible. There are interesting versions here on Youtube, such as the version of Doug McKenzie https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bD0ll-vgExA
which is certainly interesting for those looking for this song with a more complex harmony. I hope you enjoy

For the nice midi keyboard screen please visit: http://www.midiculous.com

More info about the song:
I Will Wait for You ist ein Song by Michel Legrand (Musik) and Jacques Demy, der 1964 veröffentlicht wurde.
Legrand / Demy schrieben den Song für den Musical-Film Die Regenschirme von Cherbourg (Originaltitel: Les Parapluies de Cherbourg, 1964, Regie: Jacques Demy), with Catherine Deneuve und Nino Castelnuovo in den Hauptrollen. Die Gesangsdoubles der beiden Darsteller waren Danielle Licari (für Deneuve) and José Bartel. Das Lied, dessen englischer Text von Norman Gimbel stammt, erhielt 1966 eine Oscars-Nominierung in der Kategorie Bester Song.
Die ersten beiden Zeilen des Lieds lauteten: If it takes forever, I will wait for you / For a thousand summers, I will wait for you.
I Will Wait for You erschien auf der Soundtrack-LP The Umbrellas of Cherbourg beautiful Disques Vogue. Coverversionen des Songs veröffentlichten ab Mitte der 1960er-Jahre u. to. Nancy and Frank Sinatra, Steve Lawrence (desse Version 1965 in the USA auf 113 kam), Andy Williams, Henry Mancini and Jane Morgan. Im Bereich des Jazz wurde I Will Wait for You in the Hälfte der 1960er-Jahre u. to. auch von Louis Armstrong (gleichnamiges Album auf Brunswick Records), Dukes of Dixieland, Astrud Gilbert, Helen Merrill, Oscar Peterson, Bud Shank, Gary McFarland, Benny Goodman and Donald Byrd (auf dem Blue-Note-Album The Creeper) interpretiert. Pianist Steve Kuhn nahm im Trio with George Mraz and Billy Drummond 2010 das Album I Will Wait for You - The Music of Michel Legrand auf.

Scriabin A.Prelude - op 31 no 3 Eb minor.YT_description:
Scriabin - Prelude Op. 31 no. 3 in E flat minor - Presto. Played by Tal-Haim Samnon. Tal-Haim Samnon was born in Tel Aviv in 1986. From the age of six till eighteen he took piano lessons with Mrs. Hanna Shalgi of the Givatayim Music Conservatory. Since then he studied with Prof. Arie Vardi for six years at the Buchman- Mehta school of Music in Tel Aviv University where he did his B.A. In present time he studies with Prof. Evelyne Brancart at the Jacobs School of Music in Indiana University, Bloomington. Tal graduated from the Thelma- Yellin High School for the Performing Arts and served in the Israeli Army as "distinguished musician", enabling him to pursue his musical career uninterruptedly. 
Since the age of seven he has performed at many concerts in Israel and in Europe: Germany, Austria, France, Scotland, Holland, Switzerland and Portugal and more. He often performs for the Israeli "voice of music" channel, both in live broadcasts and in recordings, and has recorded for the Dutch radio as well.
Tal has been awarded the America-Israel Cultural Foundation scholarships since 1998, the "Ronen foundation" scholarships and "Buchman-Heyman foundation" scholarship.
He has appeared with several orchestras as a soloist, such as the Thelma-Yellin Orchestra, the Kibbutzim Orchestra, the Jerusalem Symphony Orchestra, the Israeli Chamber Orchestra, the Rishon Lezion Orchestra and was a soloist at a festive gala concert with Israel Philharmonic Orchestra under Maestro Zubin Mehta, marking the opening of the Buchman Mehta College of Music in Tel-Aviv.
He has taken part in many master classes, including those at Tel Hai with internationally known pianists such as Alexander Korsantia, John O'Connor and Pnina Zaltzman, Victor Derevianko, Leslie Howrad, Peter Tackacs, Jacob Lateiner, Boris Berman, Murray Perahia and more.
He won the Turgeman competition, the Paul Ben Haim competition, the "Highlights", the Ariana Katz, the "Maurice M. Clairmont", the "Young artist", "Lions Israel ", the "Tel Hai International Master Classes Competition" and the Zubin Mehta Piano Competition.

Albeniz I.The Summer - op 101 no 2 in D.PS_title: The Summer - op 101 no 2 in D major
Albeniz I.The Summer - op 101 no 2 in D.YT_description: L'Eté (Summer) is the second movement of a suite called "Les Saisons" (The Seasons), Op. 101 by the Spanish composer Isaac Albeniz.  Albeniz wrote a lot of music in his lifetime, not all of it good, and not all of it in a Spanish mood.  This suite sort of falls somewhere in between.  It's not the best Albeniz, but I think it deserves to be played and listened to. With this recording, I have finally completed recording the whole suite.  This movement eluded me, and I still don't quite understand it.  It is the hardest and also unfortunately the weakest piece musically in the set.  I don't see anything about it that represents my idea of summer.  I had a hard time getting my head around it, and I still don't think my performance is very successful, but at least the whole suite is now available on YouTube.

Debussy - Prelude  La Danse de Puck. Tal-Haim Samnon was born in Tel Aviv in 1986. From the age of six till eighteen he took piano lessons with Mrs. Hanna Shalgi of the Givatayim Music Conservatory. Since then he studied with Prof. Arie Vardi for six years at the Buchman- Mehta school of Music in Tel Aviv University where he did his B.A. In present time he studies with Prof. Evelyne Brancart at the Jacobs School of Music in Indiana University, Bloomington. Tal graduated from the Thelma- Yellin High School for the Performing Arts and served in the Israeli Army as "distinguished musician", enabling him to pursue his musical career uninterruptedly. 
Since the age of seven he has performed at many concerts in Israel and in Europe: Germany, Austria, France, Scotland, Holland, Switzerland and Portugal and more. He often performs for the Israeli "voice of music" channel, both in live broadcasts and in recordings, and has recorded for the Dutch radio as well.
Tal has been awarded the America-Israel Cultural Foundation scholarships since 1998, the "Ronen foundation" scholarships and "Buchman-Heyman foundation" scholarship.
He has appeared with several orchestras as a soloist, such as the Thelma-Yellin Orchestra, the Kibbutzim Orchestra, the Jerusalem Symphony Orchestra, the Israeli Chamber Orchestra, the Rishon Lezion Orchestra and was a soloist at a festive gala concert with Israel Philharmonic Orchestra under Maestro Zubin Mehta, marking the opening of the Buchman Mehta College of Music in Tel-Aviv.
He has taken part in many master classes, including those at Tel Hai with internationally known pianists such as Alexander Korsantia, John O'Connor and Pnina Zaltzman, Victor Derevianko, Leslie Howrad, Peter Tackacs, Jacob Lateiner, Boris Berman, Murray Perahia and more.
He won the Turgeman competition, the Paul Ben Haim competition, the "Highlights", the Ariana Katz, the "Maurice M. Clairmont", the "Young artist", "Lions Israel ", the "Tel Hai International Master Classes Competition" and the Zubin Mehta Piano Competition.

Coulthard J.Piano Sonata No 2.YT_description:
Jean Coulthard, OC, OBC (February 10, 1908 - March 9, 2000) was a Canadian composer and music educator. She was part of a trio of women composers who dominated Western Canadian music in the twentieth century: Coulthard, Barbara Pentland, and Violet Archer. All three died within weeks of each other in 2000. Her own work might be loosely termed "prematurely neo-Romantic", as the orthodox serialists who dominated academic musical life in North America during the 1950s and 1960s had little use for her. Some of her well-known compositions include Cradle Song, Threnody, Canadian Fantasy, Ballade "A Winter's Tale" and her opera Return of the Native.

Jane Coop is one of the most in demand and established pianists Canada has ever produced. With performances in halls around the world, she consistently engages audiences with her inspired performances and exhilarating programming. She has toured extensively throughout North America, Britain, Western and Eastern Europe, Russia. She toured Asia in 1994, performing in Japan, China, and Hong Kong. She has appeared as recitalist or soloist in, among other places, New York, London, Washington, Moscow, Paris, Warsaw, Brussels, Budapest, Kiev, St. Petersburg, Prague, Utrecht, Beijing and Tokyo.

Easton M.Conversations.YT_description:
Rebecca Chambers - piano
Michael Easton writes:
I wrote this work very late at night after dinner in a crowded restaurant where everybody else's conversations seemed so much more interesting than the one I was enduring. The piece attempts to conjure up the prattle of others and the odd snatch of half-comprehensible conversation.
This bagatelle was written for Ronald Farren-Price for a tour of Russia in 1988. One of Australia's most brilliant younger pianists, Rebecca Chambers, performs the work on this recording.

Bonis M.March Militaire Op 92 No 5.YT_description: Mélanie Hélène Bonis (1858-1937) was born in Paris, France.  Self-taught from a young age, she attended the Paris Conservatory at age 16.  Studied composition with Ernest Guiraud, organ with César Frank, and attended classes with Debussy.  At the Conservatoire, she won first prize in harmony and second in accompanying.  Pressure from parents forced her to withdraw.  In 1883 she married Albert Domange and spent the majority of her time caring for her family.  Most of her compositions were started after 1894 and were written in the late romantic style.  She wrote for solo piano, organ, choral, orchestra, and pedagogical compositions.  Because women were not afforded as many opportunities she changed her first name to Mel under which all of her compositions were published.

Bertini H.Study in D major Op 100 No 10.PS_title: Study in D major Op 100 No 10
Bertini H.Study in D major Op 100 No 10.YT_description:
I learned this piece for the Piano Jam #75 in r\piano subreddit. I was looking for something I could learn in a week, to continue my self imposing challenge of recording a new piece every week. I didn't know these etudes, it is interesting because Bertini wrote 25 easy progressive etudes in his Op.100, just like Burgmuller (25 etudes in the same opus). I wonder who inspired who.

This piece is basically an etude for the week fingers in the right hand and the challenges are maintaining rhythmic uniformity while playing relatively fast, in legato, dolce, and forte. It is a good idea to use wrist rotation to play the notes, instead of relying on finger movements alone, so this piece was good for practicing that technique (which I am not good at). The suggested tempo for this piece is 184 BPM for the quarter note, which is quite fast. I did reach that tempo while I was practicing but I didn't like how it sounded. I chose a much slower tempo for this recording, at about 150 BPM. 

I think my interpretation is ok, considering that this is almost an exercise, not being very elaborate musically. But when I was recording I realized that I was not playing the articulation in the end correctly, doing all notes legato when there is a "slur separation" before the notes in the last tempo of each measure. It was too late to change, I couldn't do that articulation on the spot, but there is not much difference anyway.

The recording was made using a pair of condenser microphones, AKG P170, placed above the top lid of my upright piano, a Kawai K200.

A funny little piece, with the left hand chasing the right hand. 

Recorded on 2 August 2017.

This recording was made after initially learning the piece. I have not memorized it, hence the need to read from the score while playing. Having only learned it once, there are inevitably things I'd have liked to play differently. I do not claim that this is the way this piece is to be played, nor do I encourage people to copy what I did. I merely record and post this for keeping track of my own progress as a piano player.

Geraghty J.Harrys Rag.YT_description:
Harry's Rag - Written and performed by John Geraghty. Harry's Rag is featured in Pianist Magazine - Issue 110 (Oct-Nov 2019). 
#greenolivepublications

Small facts:

This fun little number is paying homage to Scott Joplin’s The Entertainer which was the theme music in the 1973 film The Sting starring Robert Redford and Paul Newman. 

Practice Tip: 

Once you’ve learnt the notes without looking down at the keyboard, set the metronome so that the click is played on every quaver in the bass clef. That way the quavers will ‘act’ like crotchets and the semiquavers will ‘act’ and feel like quavers. Gradually increase the tempo by no more than 5 on the metronome. Your fingers won’t feel the speed increase. Keep doing this until you reach 160 then halve the metronome speed to 80, back to a crotchet click and keep increasing the tempo by 5 until you reach 100. If you find your fingers lifting up, decrease the speed and stay at that tempo for at least a week to give your fingers time to adjust to the new tempo.

Hazel Nguyen began her music education at the age of three. Developing a controlled, prodigious technique, she has been praised for her authority over the most complex technically demanding pieces, the depth of her musical insight and charismatic stage presence. 
With a full scholarship to study at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland, she graduated with a First-Class Bachelor Degree in Joint-Principal Conducting and Piano Performance. At the Royal College of Music, she achieved Master of Music with Distinction in Piano Performance. 
Currently, Hazel is teaching at Rossall School in Lancashire and Sedbergh School in Cumbria, as well as judging competitions and performing worldwide. She is also one of the youngest examiners for ABRSM in the UK.
In addition, Hazel is a recording artist for Tomplay in Switzerland, a transcriber, an arranger and business partner for Musescore UK.
You can find her latest videos here https://www.youtube.com/user/hazel20111993/ 
In the past, Hazel was awarded Worthing Pianist of The Year. At Brighton Springboard Music Festival, she won the Senior Championship, as well as the Senior Concerto Class. As a result, she will be performing with Brighton Orchestra in the next seasons. 
Her virtuosic recording of Beethoven’s Bagatelle op.33 no.5 was played on BBC Radio 3 and made signature for their program In Tune. In Glasgow, producing the best performance of a Mozart Concerto, she was awarded Jock Holden Memorial Trophy. Hazel won the Rosanne Archibald prize for the most promising musician at Blackburn Music Festival and was also a winner at Glasgow Rising Star competition.

Nghệ sĩ piano Hazel Nguyen, tên đầy đủ là Nguyễn Ngọc Trà My, bắt đầu học nhạc từ năm ba tuổi. Kỹ thuật trên phím đàn của cô được cho là xuất sắc. Với học bổng toàn phần trao tặng bởi Học Viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Scotland năm 2012, cô đã tốt nghiệp chuyên ngành Piano và Chỉ Huy Dàn Nhạc với tấm bằng hạng nhất. Ngay sau đó, Hazel đã tốt nghiệp thạc sĩ chuyên ngành biểu diễn Piano tại Học viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Anh. 
Hiện tại, Hazel đang giảng dạy tại trường Rossall thuộc hạt Lancashire và trường Sedbergh tại hạt Cumbria, Anh Quốc. Gần đây, cô là nghệ sĩ thu âm cho hãng Tomplay của Thụy Sĩ, và cũng là  một nhà soạn nhạc và phát triển cho ứng dụng Musescore ở Anh.

Những năm qua, Hazel được trao giải Nghệ sĩ piano danh giá của năm tại Worthing. Tại Liên hoan âm nhạc Brighton Springboard, cô đã giành giải nhất tại 3 hạng mục khác nhau, cũng như giải nhất cuộc thi Concerto. Cô sẽ biểu diễn cùng Dàn nhạc Brighton trong các mùa diễn tiếp theo. 
Bản thu âm Beethoven Bagatelle op.33/5 của cô đã phát trên BBC Radio 3 và được dùng làm nhạc nền chính cho chương trình In Tune của họ. Tại Glasgow, nhờ màn trình diễn thuyết phục của Mozart Concerto số 12 cung La trưởng, Hazel đã chiến thắng với Cúp tưởng niệm Jock Holden dành cho người chơi Mozart xuất sắc nhất. Cô cũng là người chiến thắng tại cuộc thi Ngôi sao đang lên của Glasgow. Hazel còn giành giải thưởng Rosanne Archibald cho nghệ sĩ triển vọng nhất tại Blackburn Music Festival.

Grieg E.At Your Cradle - op 68 no 5 E ma.YT_description:
Edvard Grieg - Lyric Pieces, Op.68 No.5 Bådnlåt (At the Cradle)

I've long had a soft spot for Grieg's music, sometimes its simplicity and straight-forward nature can infer a certain mawkish sentimentality, but really I think it often conveys a sense of starkness, vulnerability and delicate intimacy. In this Lyric Piece, I often picture a parental figure quietly engaged in loving dialogue with a child, gentle assurances of safety and warmth but with whispered intimations of what difficulties might lie ahead. Gradually moving from one stage of dreaming to the next, until finally passing the threshold into sound sleep.

Liszt F.Consolation in Db major No 3 fro.YT_description:
Hmm... what to say about this one. It has a quality sort of like a Nocturne or Mendelsohn's songs without words. It's in a major Key but still there's something tragic about it. Mysterious qualities in art paired with instantly gratifying qualities really leave an impression. I remember first practicing this and thinking to myself, "man, once this one hits the streets, I'll really be turning heads." I'm not sure if it's left an impression like that. But I do think people have enjoyed it. 

I suppose more than anything else I hear Liszt's over dramatic self speaking of a love he lost. I know people tend to hate that side of Liszt, the overly dramatic yearning. And I just as much as anyone, hate phony crap. But for some reason, I never minded Liszt's drama. I mean, I guess the fact of the matter is, Love can make you feel all sorts of intense emotions even though no one has died and you'll probably get over it. There are a lot of fish in the sea. But still I can identify with these feelings and there's no point in denying their existence. So Yearn away... tug at my heart strings and make me feel an empty hole in my existence that perhaps only chocolate can fill. Heh...

Scriabin A.Prelude - op 17 no 6 Bb major.YT_description: The great choreographer, Martha Clarke and I collaborated on a project called Vers la flamme 20 years ago; short stories of Anton Chekhov set to selected piano music of the great Russian pianist/composer/synesthete, Alexander Scriabin. Martha and I spent long nights at her benevolently haunted Connecticut home reading through Scriabin works, favorite and newly discovered, and such is the immediately evocative and poetic power of Scriabin's music that Martha would immediately upon first measures, opine: "oh, that's perfect for Lady With a Lapdog; that's great for The Grasshopper." We did the show on Broadway at the Victory Theater (where I finally met my brother-from-another-mother, Victor Garber, an old friend of Martha's) at Jacob's Pillow, American Dance Festival, and at the Kennedy Center. I shared the stage with five incredible dancers and one precocious Pomeranian, Sophie. Subsequently, I recorded the show's dozens of pieces for a record Ransom Wilson produced and Paul Blakemore engineered in the incredibly atmospheric Methuen Music Hall, a marble-floored room housing a huge pipe organ, a room much taller than it was wide; perfect ambience for the opulence and magic of Scriabin. This video I recorded on The World's Greatest Steinway Concert Grand in my home a few nights ago. I came to know this particular early Scriabin Prelude long before Martha and I met; it was a favorite of my master teacher, Russell Sherman. With its sentimental torch-song octave leap at its apotheosis, he referred to it affectionately as the Judy Garland Prelude; apt and I'll always think if it so. I'll be doing quite a lot of home recording in the coming months; first these Scriabin offerings, and then likely a few of my arrangements that haven't been commercially released; some Radiohead, Tears for Fears, a Sondheim favorite for my friend, Sara and some others. Korn U.Caballos Espanoles.YT_description:
"Caballos Españoles" by Uwe Korn from "Tango Meets Jazz" for piano, based on "Por una Cabeza" by Carlos Gardel. Schott Music ED 20878D (... sorry for the spelling mistake in the video). Recorded by Uwe Korn at Bauer Studios in 2010. 
Youtube playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLgE3tT1gNOJErtaUN24Z61XyHe20hplRI

Sheet Music:
https://shop.abrsm.org/shop/powersearch/powersearch_results?search=tango+meets+jazz&x=0&y=0

https://www.halleonard.com/product/49018387/tango-meets-jazz

 https://de.schott-music.com/uwe-korn
and wherever you can buy sheet music.


Tango is not just a „classic“ dance form: more than that, it almost represents an approach to life. In any case, it involves plunging into a maelstrom of emotions. Ten tangos are brought together in this book, including popular pieces such as “Jalousie”, “El Cholco”, “Por una Cabeza” and modern classics such as “Adiós Nonino” by Astor Piazolla. These piano arrangements aim to do justice to the special sound qualities of the tango, with a jazzy piece presented alongside each tango. In most cases, the preceding tango is reinterpreted in a jazz-related style, though some are paired with new composition. Whether it is an arrangement or a new composition, the idea always comes from the tango. For instance, the corn cob (“El Choclo”) is made into a corn dish with a tangy sauce (“Choclo con Salsa”), while fiery jealousy (“Jalousie”) serves to light a Cuban cigar (“Le Cigare Jaloux”). An unhappy lover tries his luck at the races (“Por una Cabeza”), where he might be advised to bet on Spanish horses (“Caballos Españoles”). Astor Piazolla wrote his piece “Adiós Nonino” after the death of his father: jazzing this up would be totally inappropriate. The “Preludio del Ángel” that follows it is a new compositions inspired by Piazolla and Bach.

Over the years 1825–1849, Frédéric Chopin wrote at least 69 mazurkas, based on the traditional Polish dance.The serial numbering of the 58 published mazurkas normally goes only up to 51. The remaining 7 are referred to by their key or catalogue number. His composition of these mazurkas signaled new ideas of nationalism, and influenced and inspired other composers—mostly eastern Europeans—to support their national music.

Origins 

Chopin based his mazurkas on the traditional Polish folk dance, also called the mazurka (or "mazur" in Polish). However, while Chopin used the traditional mazurka as his model, he was able to transform his mazurkas into an entirely new genre, one that became known as a "Chopin genre".

Musical style

Since Chopin's mazurkas connect to an already established genre of music, some of the characteristics of that genre (the traditional Polish mazurka) remain the same in his interpretation of the genre. For example, both the traditional mazurka and Chopin's version contain a great deal of repetition. This can mean repetition of a single measure or small group of measures, repetition of a theme, or even repetition of an entire section. This repetition makes sense in the traditional dance for the repeat of a certain section of the actual dance; even though Chopin did not compose his mazurkas so they could be danced to, it is clear Chopin kept the original form in mind. Furthermore, many of the rhythmic patterns of the traditional mazurka also appear in Chopin's compositions so they still convey the idea of a dance, but a more "self-contained, stylized dance piece." In keeping with this idea, Chopin did try to make his mazurkas more technically interesting by furthering their chromaticism and harmony, along with using classical techniques, such as counterpoint and fugues. In fact, Chopin used more classical techniques in his mazurkas than in any of his other genres. One of these techniques is four part harmony in the manner of a chorale.

Influences

While it is known that Chopin's mazurkas are connected to the traditional dance, throughout the years there has been much scholarly debate as to how exactly they are connected. The main subject of this debate is whether Chopin had an actual direct connection to Polish folk music, or whether he heard Polish national music in urban areas and was inspired by that to compose his mazurkas.

Hassler J.Ecossaise in G major Op 38 No.YT_description:
ABRSM Piano 2021 2022 Grade 2 A3  Hassler Ecossaise in G No  23 from 50 pièces à l’usage des commençans, Op  38 by Hampstead Piano Academy.


Johann Wilhelm Hässler (1747-1822) was a German composer and keyboard player. His education follows the heritage of Bach, as his teacher studied with him. He lived and worked in Russia as both, performer and teacher.


Ecossaise in G (No. 23 from 50 pièces à l'usage des commençans, Op. 38) is a folk dance originated in Scotland. Hässler wrote it for his students but he is not the only author to use Ecossaises for teaching, as there are other composers such as Beethoven who also taught these pieces in his lessons.

Beach A.Columbine Op 25 No 2.YT_description:
"Columbine," a charming waltz composed by the remarkable American composer Amy Beach, stands as one of the delightful pieces in her suite "Children's Carnival." Crafted in 1894, this miniature masterpiece is a testament to Beach's compositional prowess and her dedication to nurturing the musical talents of young pianists. The suite, comprised of six enchanting movements, takes inspiration from the characters of early European pantomime, which enjoyed popularity in America during the late 19th century. "Columbine" is a vivacious portrayal of one of these captivating characters.

One of the remarkable aspects of "Children's Carnival" is its purpose as a teaching tool for young pianists. Amy Beach's compositions often sought to encourage musical education and exploration, and this suite is a perfect embodiment of that mission. "Columbine" and the other movements provide young musicians with the opportunity to develop their technical skills while immersing themselves in the world of storytelling through music.

If you'd like to learn more about American composers like Amy Beach, please visit:

https://www.americanpianomusic.com/

If you like what you hear, please consider supporting my work by purchasing one of my solo piano albums at:

Jan Ladislav Dussek - Sonatina in G major op.20 no. 1

Jan Ladislav Dussek (baptized Jan Václav Dusík, with surname also written as Duschek or Düssek; 12 February 1760 – 20 March 1812) was a Czech composer and pianist. He was an important representative of Czech music abroad in the second half of the 18th century and the beginning of the 19th century. Some of his more forward-looking piano works have traits often associated with Romanticism.

Dussek was one of the first piano virtuosos to travel widely throughout Europe. He performed at courts and concert venues from London to Saint Petersburg to Milan, and was celebrated for his technical prowess. During a nearly ten-year stay in London, he was instrumental in extending the size of the pianoforte, and was the recipient of one of John Broadwood's first 6-octave pianos, CC-c4. Harold Schonberg wrote that he was the first pianist to sit at the piano with his profile to the audience, earning him the appellation "le beau visage." All subsequent pianists have sat on stage in this manner. He was one of the best-regarded pianists in Europe before Beethoven's rise to prominence.

Burgmuller J.F.The Pearls Op 109 No 2.YT_description:
Friedrich Burgmüller - Les Perles op.109 n. 2
Fausto Bongelli, piano
Friedrich Burgmüller, in Paris known under the French form of his name, Frédéric, was born in Regensburg in 1806, the son of the composer, pianist and music teacher Johann August Franz Burgmüller, and elder brother of the composer, conductor and pianist Norbert Burgmüller. Friedrich Burgmüller was taught by his father. After the latter’s death in 1824 he followed him as director of music in Düsseldorf, teaching music in Mühlhausen and as a cellist in Basel. In 1832 he settled in Paris, where he won a considerable reputation as a piano teacher, and internationally as a composer of salon pieces and studies. He did much to promote the work of his brother Norbert, four years his junior, whose career had been cut short by his sudden death at the spa in Aachen in 1836. Friedrich Burgmüller’s activities brought continued success in Paris. Many of his compositions proved successful among amateurs, for whom his pieces offered limited technical challenges, coupled with the satisfaction of musical interest. His Études (‘Studies’) have continued to provide a basis for piano teaching and the development of technical proficiency.

From the liner notes for "Tunes for Mademoiselle" :  

"The Blue Gardenia was written for John Martin by master miniaturist Phillip Wilcher and is a beautiful example of a piano blues, representing a slight change of direction for this most romantic of Australian composers. It is simple and uncluttered, displaying Wilcher's great ability to write music free of excess that is always attractive and engaging."

Bless you John for playing my piece so beautifully!

Burgmuller J.F.Studies Op 105 No 4.YT_description:
Phillip Sear plays a Czerny-like study by the German composer Friedrich Burgmüller (1806-74).
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#4 from 12 études brillantes et mélodiques pour piano, Op. 105 (c. 1853)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The German composer (Johann) Friedrich Burgmüller (1806-74) trained in his own country but moved to France in 1832, and settled there, becoming a French citizen. He was a successful piano teacher and composer of salon pieces and studies. This piece, from Burgmüller's set of 18 characteristic Études, Op 109, strikes me as very similar in musical style to the studies in Czerny's 'Art of Finger Dexterity', Op. 740.

Gillock W.Blue Mood.YT_description:
William Gillock (1917-1993), noted music educator and composer of piano music, was born in LaRussell, Missouri, where he learned to play the piano at an early age. After graduating from Central Methodist College, his musical career led him to long tenures in New Orleans, Louisiana and Dallas, Texas, where he was always in great demand as a teacher, clinician, and composer. Called the "Schubert of children's composers" in tribute to his extraordinary melodic gift, Gillock composed numerous solos and ensembles for students of all levels. He was honored on multiple occasions by the National Federation of Music Clubs (NFMC) with the Award of Merit for Service to American Music, and his music continues to be remarkably popular throughout the United States and throughout the world.

Kabalevsky D.Cradle Song No 8 from 30 Pi.YT_description:
Kabalevsky Op. 27 no. 8 Cradle Song
Kabalevsky maintains a mysterious nocturnal mood throughout this lullaby (I love those beautiful seventh chords).  Bring out the melody as it travels between the hands.  Notice that when the melody returns to the right hand in measure 32 it's an inversion of the first entrance in measure 3.  At this point, you might be wondering "what sort of childhood did Kabalevsky have?"  Of the first ten selection, 7 are written in a minor key and some are downright gloomy.

⭐ツェルニー100番について

ツェルニー100番においてはほぼペダルは使わず、指でのレガートを意識しています。
それは小さい頃から必ず意識したほうが良いことです。
この練習曲集において、速く適当に弾いてしまうことは何よりも危険です。とにかくゆっくり丁寧に、自分の音を聞きながら弾くことを絶対に推奨します（我が生徒たちにも口酸っぱく言っていることです）

私自身、今回演奏する際に何よりも重視したのは丁寧さです。実は速く弾くことよりもゆっくり弾くことのほうが難しかったりします。ぜひ皆様も、ゆっくり丁寧に自分の音を聞きながら練習してみてくださいね😉🎵

ーーーー

小さい頃から大好きだったツェルニー。
今では教える立場となり、「教えるために弾く」場面が増え、その魅力を再認識する日々を送っていました。
嫌いな方も多いツェルニーですが、私は先生の演奏やピアニストのCDに憧れ、こんな風に弾けるようになりたい…！と、一生懸命に練習していた気がします。今の時代非常に便利な動画でツェルニーを見て、楽しく練習してもらえたら。ツェルニーのことを大好きになってもらえたら。そんな気持ちを込めて、演奏いたしました。

手首や指の使い方が一番伝わりやすいアングルで撮ったつもりでおります。音だけでなく、フィジカルな面での使い方も是非、参考にしていただければ嬉しいです。

Estevez A.Cancion para dormir una muneca.YT_description:
Canción para dormir una muñeca
Lullaby for a Doll
No. 7 from 17 piezas infantiles (17 Children Pieces)
by Antonio Estévez (1916-88)

Antonio Estévez was a Venezuelan composer, conductor and oboist.  From 1934 to 1944 he studied oboe and composition at the School of Music and Declamation in Caracas, and played the oboe in the Venezuela Symphony Orchestra.  During the Second World War, he also taught at the Nation School of Music in Caracas.  After the war, he studied with Bernstein, Koussevitzky and others at Columbia University and Tanglewood.  Estévez's earlier music was nationalistic in style, inspired by Venezuelan music and culture.  From 1961 he adopted new orchestral and electroacoustic tenchiques, after studying electronic music in Paris.  He also worked closely with kinetic painters Jesus Soto and Carlos Cruz Diez, and created multimedia works, including a 'sonic space' for the Jesus Soto Museum in Venezuela.

Hengeveld G.Blues from Melodie en Rhythm.YT_description:
This is the most popular piece from Gerard Hengeveld's collection of ten pieces in popular styles called 'Melodie en Rhythme'. It was published in Holland in 1961 at a time when teaching pieces in jazz or pop genres were very thin on the ground. I have played it here at a speed close to the composer's metronome marking of crochet = 80 (actually even slower than my tempo). Many would prefer it faster. It is not a conventional twelve bar blues in form but divides into three eight bar phrases (ABA). 


Interestingly this is one of those ABRSM pieces which have appeared in different exam grade lists at different times. In 1978 (!) it was listed as a grade 5 piece but in 2012 it was set for grade 4. I would put it mid way between: a bit short and a little too easy for grade 5 perhaps.

Hazel Nguyen began her music education at the age of three. Developing a controlled, prodigious technique, she has been praised for her authority over the most complex technically demanding pieces, the depth of her musical insight and charismatic stage presence. 
With a full scholarship to study at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland, she graduated with a First-Class Bachelor Degree in Joint-Principal Conducting and Piano Performance. At the Royal College of Music, she achieved Master of Music with Distinction in Piano Performance. 
Currently, Hazel is teaching at Rossall School in Lancashire and Sedbergh School in Cumbria, as well as judging competitions and performing worldwide. She is also one of the youngest examiners for ABRSM in the UK.
In addition, Hazel is a recording artist for Tomplay in Switzerland, a transcriber, an arranger and business partner for Musescore UK.
You can find her latest videos here https://www.youtube.com/user/hazel20111993/ 
In the past, Hazel was awarded Worthing Pianist of The Year. At Brighton Springboard Music Festival, she won the Senior Championship, as well as the Senior Concerto Class. As a result, she will be performing with Brighton Orchestra in the next seasons. 
Her virtuosic recording of Beethoven’s Bagatelle op.33 no.5 was played on BBC Radio 3 and made signature for their program In Tune. In Glasgow, producing the best performance of a Mozart Concerto, she was awarded Jock Holden Memorial Trophy. Hazel won the Rosanne Archibald prize for the most promising musician at Blackburn Music Festival and was also a winner at Glasgow Rising Star competition. 
------------------------
Nghệ sĩ piano Hazel Nguyen, tên đầy đủ là Nguyễn Ngọc Trà My, bắt đầu học nhạc từ năm ba tuổi. Kỹ thuật trên phím đàn của cô được cho là xuất sắc. Hazel thường được khen ngợi vì chinh phục thành công những tác phẩm đòi hỏi kỹ thuật phức tạp nhất, chiều sâu âm nhạc sâu lắng nhất, và trên hết là những màn biểu diễn lôi cuốn của cô. 
Với học bổng toàn phần trao tặng bởi Học Viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Scotland năm 2012, cô đã tốt nghiệp chuyên ngành Piano và Chỉ Huy Dàn Nhạc với tấm bằng hạng nhất. Ngay sau đó, Hazel đã tốt nghiệp thạc sĩ chuyên ngành biểu diễn Piano tại Học viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Anh. 
Hiện tại, Hazel đang giảng dạy tại trường Rossall thuộc hạt Lancashire và trường Sedbergh tại hạt Cumbria, Anh Quốc. Cô cũng tham gia các hoạt động biểu diễn và làm giám khảo cho các cuộc thi âm nhạc trong nước và quốc tế. Thêm vào đó, Hazel là một trong những thành viên trẻ nhất của hội đồng chấm thi âm nhạc hoàng gia Anh ABRSM.
Gần đây, cô là nghệ sĩ thu âm cho hãng Tomplay của Thụy Sĩ, và cũng là  một nhà soạn nhạc và phát triển cho ứng dụng Musescore ở Anh.
Bạn có thể tìm thấy những video của Hazel tại https://www.youtube.com/user/hazel20111993/ 
Những năm qua, Hazel được trao giải Nghệ sĩ piano danh giá của năm tại Worthing. Tại Liên hoan âm nhạc Brighton Springboard, cô đã giành giải nhất tại 3 hạng mục khác nhau, cũng như giải nhất cuộc thi Concerto. Cô sẽ biểu diễn cùng Dàn nhạc Brighton trong các mùa diễn tiếp theo. 
Bản thu âm Beethoven Bagatelle op.33/5 của cô đã phát trên BBC Radio 3 và được dùng làm nhạc nền chính cho chương trình In Tune của họ. Tại Glasgow, nhờ màn trình diễn thuyết phục của Mozart Concerto số 12 cung La trưởng, Hazel đã chiến thắng với Cúp tưởng niệm Jock Holden dành cho người chơi Mozart xuất sắc nhất. Cô cũng là người chiến thắng tại cuộc thi Ngôi sao đang lên của Glasgow. Hazel còn giành giải thưởng Rosanne Archibald cho nghệ sĩ triển vọng nhất tại Blackburn Music Festival.

For more "Modern Waltzes", please check out the playlist https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLIaVIXV8ILjnLE1pAhM1EmgxKEOc7LRqc

Any requests for scores, please follow the instructions in my profile. Follow this link to my profile: http://tinyurl.com/h9vnpuw

It is difficult to define what a "Modern Waltz" is. I will include waltzes written mainly in the 20th and 21th  centuries, which do not conform to the classical Viennese, French and English Waltz styles, and where the melodies and harmonies are more adventurous.

Dmitri Dmitriyevich Shostakovich (25 September 1906 – 9 August 1975) was one of Soviet Russia's most prominent concert pianist and composer in the 20th century. Although he achieved his fame under the Soviets, he had a stormy relationship with them, and his music was criticized and condemned by them for being unconventional.

The Barrel Organ Waltz is one of the pieces written by Shostakovich as incidental music for the Soviet movie The Gadfly. The most famous piece from this suite is the Romance : https://youtu.be/Zw7YM8S2A9k. 

The Barrel Organ Waltz is a very charming and happy piece, with a carnival like atmosphere. The original piece was written for the orchestra, and this is a transcription of it for the piano.

Copland A.Midsummer Nocturne.YT_description:
Some thoughts on this little gem:

"Technically, the midsummer festival is in late June, but this little piece always reminds me of how it felt to be a kid during this particular time of year. It's the last few days of July, and hot as can be. Your parents know that school is coming, but for you, since August hasn't hit yet, school still feels like an eternity away. Good thing, too: you need to focus on the important things, like running around the backyard and helping your siblings and cousins catch as many lightning bugs as possible."

Scarlatti D.Sonata in E minor K 198.YT_description:
www.szaluckapiano.com

Domenico Scarlatti's keyboard sonatas is a group of 555 sonatas for harpsichord, dating from the early 18th century. Scarlatti, though born in Naples, spent nearly 40 years with the royal courts in the Iberian Peninsula, first with the Portuguese royal family, then in Spain when Portuguese princess Maria Barbara de Bragança (for whom he had been music master) married the Spanish crown prince Fernando (later Ferdinand VI). The sonatas show a mastery of keyboard technique equal to that of Scarlatti’s contemporary Johann Sebastian Bach, with elaborately decorated phrases.

Scarlatti’s sonatas did not come to publication in an orderly fashion, making it difficult to determine the order of their composition. Several music historians have sought to organize this mass of music, each using different criteria. As a result, several numbering systems are in use. The most common system was established in the 1950s by American musicologist Ralph Kirkpatrick, in which Scarlatti works are designated by numbers preceded by the letter K.

Betsy Schwarm - Britannica.com

Maykapar S.Toccatina No 1 from Trifles O.YT_description:
Here's a little serie for any students or amateur who wants to hear intermediate pieces.

Its a grade 6 piece, with a fast moving right hand and a singing left hand. Listening to you left hand while playing will help you have a beautifull phasing and a light right hand.

Practice it slowly with a lot of articulation with a crisp right hand. 
Then,  when you play it faster try not to accentuate the beats, so we always hear the long musical phrase. 

Samouïl Maïkapar is a Russian romantic composer, pianist and teacher, born in 1867 and died in 1938.

There are a number of excellent published arrangements for piano of this well known Lied (song) by Schubert in the public domain.  This video features an arrangement by August Horn.  You can play the arrangement as written or add your own ideas as you go along, as many performers do today.

The sheet music is free to download from the IMSLP Music Library.  
https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/23/IMSLP24143-PMLP02204-Franz_Schubert_-_Schwanengesang_(transcr._Horn).pdf

*Note: The PDF you will download from this link is a complete album called "Schwanengesang”.  On the main page select the "Arrangements and Transcriptions" tab and scroll down to "For Piano solo (Horn)" the famous Serenade is page 15-17.

Soler A.Sonata in D minor R 25.YT_description:
The piece is on the alternative list A and makes for an exciting and not particularly polyphonic Baroque option, though students will need to polish their ornaments carefully.  I have recorded the Scarlatti option too for this grade: https://soundcloud.com/charles-tebbs/scarlatti214

How to play 18th century music from the Iberian Peninsula?  The truth is nobody knows, but both Soler and Scarlatti are coloured by folk influences, heard here especially in the second half with the flourishes and wild modulations.  If harpsichord-touch with its possibility for agogic emphasis was in part transferred to the early piano then it could have sounded a bit like this.  Add to this the sense of contrast between the various themes and the drama of the LH octaves and the pianist is left with a conundrum of whether to fuse everything within a single unbending rhythm or to characterise each of the various themes with its own rhythmic lilt.  I go for the latter as it brings out a fun element which can easily be missed. After all, Scarlatti, who may have been one of Soler's teachers, is quoted as saying his own Sonatas were 'an ingenious jesting with art.'

See also this version on harpsichord: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=57ipzhZLKXs

Year of composition: 1870

Painting: Flowering Orchard - Camille Pissarro

Alexis Emmanuel Chabrier (January 18, 1841 – September 13, 1894) was a French Romantic composer and pianist. Although known primarily for two of his orchestral works, España and Joyeuse marche, he left an important corpus of operas (including L'étoile), songs, and piano music. He was admired by composers as diverse as Debussy, Ravel, Richard Strauss, Satie, Schmitt, Stravinsky, and the group of composers known as Les six. Stravinsky alluded to España in his ballet Petrushka; Gustav Mahler called España "the beginnings of modern music" and alluded to the "Dance Villageoise" in the Rondo Burleske movement of his Ninth Symphony. Ravel wrote that the opening bars of Le roi malgré lui changed the course of harmony in France, Poulenc wrote a biography of the composer, and Richard Strauss conducted the first staged performance of Chabrier's incomplete opera Briséïs. (from https://en.wikipedia.org/)

Beach A.Farewell Summer Op. 102 No.1.YT_description:
Amy Marcy Beach (Mrs. H. H. A. Beach) - Farewell, Summer
from 2 Piano Pieces op102 (1924)

Thomas Ang, piano
St Olave's Hart Street, 4th November 2020

------------------------------------------------

Amy Beach was widowed in 1910 and lost her mother early in 1911. After a period of mourning, she undertook European performances where she was lauded as a composer of top rank - despite naysayers saying her music was no longer fashionable. That same opinion held even when she returned to America and lived in New England; regardless, she used her status and reputation as America's leading female composer to promote the careers of young musicians. 

Even with family and friends dying around her, she continued participating in American and European musical life, publishing works past Op. 150 - all of which show an advanced command of tonal harmony, with some very adventurous effects she had clearly picked up while she was travelling in Europe.

This piece, aptly titled "Farewell, Summer", is a turn towards the past entirely suited to the neoclassical aesthetic sweeping Europe at that time. A gavotte in a simple ABA + coda form, the harmonies are rather bitter and the dissonances are quite cleverly worked out. This description, accurate though it is, does little justice to the piece itself, which packs a wonderful emotional punch.
