лауреат международных конкурсов,
лауреат молодёжной премии «Триумф»,
лауреат премии Президента РФ для молодых деятелей культуры, 
солистка МГАФ
Екатерина Мечетина является на сегодняшний день одной из самых талантливых и ярких молодых пианисток мирового уровня. Она выступает с лучшими оркестрами России и Европы. Ей посчастливилось работать с великими современными музыкантами. Родион Щедрин, впервые услышав Екатерину, доверил ей мировую премьеру своего Шестого фортепианного концерта. Выступления Екатерины Мечетиной всегда проходят с неизменным успехом. Слушателей покоряет не только виртуозное исполнительское мастерство пианистки, но и её удивительное обаяние.
Выступает на всемирно известных сценах, таких, как Большой, Малый и Рахманиновский залы Московской консерватории, Большой и Камерный залы Московского Дома Музыки, Концертный зал им. Чайковского, Большой театр; Concertgebouw (Амстердам), Yamaha Hall, Casals hall (Токио), Konzerthaus (Берлин), Theatre des Champs-Elysees, Salle Gaveau (Париж), Большой зал Миланской консерватории и Auditorium (Милан), Sala Patricia Meireles (Рио-де-Жанейро), Alice Tully Hall (Нью-Йорк) и др.
В её пианистической карьере огромную роль сыграли 3 выдающихся музыканта: скрипач и дирижёр Владимир Спиваков, который постоянно приглашает её в свои концерты (в разное время она выступала с «Виртуозами Москвы», Национальным филармоническим оркестром России, Российским национальным оркестром, когда им руководил В.Спиваков), виолончелист и дирижёр Мстислав Ростропович и композитор Родион Щедрин. Его новые сочинения Екатерина представляла в Москве и Амстердаме. «Благодаря этим встречам, — говорит пианистка, — я стала совершенно по-другому относиться к профессии, а каждый такой концерт для меня — событие, запоминающееся на всю жизнь».
В обширном репертуаре Екатерины более 45 концертов для фортепиано с оркестром, многие из которых были исполнены под управлением В.Спивакова, М.Ростроповича, С.Сондецкиса, Ю.Симонова, П.Когана, Д.Ситковецкого, А.Сладковского, А.Скульского и многих других выдающихся дирижеров.
Она принимала участие в крупных международных фестивалях, включая всемирно известный фестиваль «Декабрьские вечера Святослава Рихтера» в Москве, фестиваль в Дубровнике (Хорватия), а также фестиваль «Crescendo» в Москве, Санкт-Петербурге, Екатеринбурге, Пскове, Тюмени, Париже, Риге.
С 2003 года участвует в международном музыкальном проекте "Российские музы - миру".
Имеет записи на радио и ТВ России, США, Италии, Японии, Бразилии, Кувейта. В 2005 году на бельгийском лейбле «Fuga Libera» вышел её первый сольный диск с произведениями Рахманинова.
Помимо сольных выступлений Е.Мечетина часто музицирует в ансамблях разного состава. Пианистка постоянно сотрудничает с яркими молодыми российскими исполнителями - Н.Борисоглебским, С.Антоновым, Б.Андриановым, А.Огринчуком и другими.
В 2003 году была удостоена престижной молодёжной премии «Триумф».
Лауреат премии фонда "Российские музы - миру" и Министерства иностранных дел РФ - "За формирование объективного образа России на мировой арене".
C 2009 года преподаёт в Московской государственной консерватории (ассистент профессора Мндоянца А.А.) Лауреат Премии Президента РФ для молодых деятелей культуры за 2010 год. Член Совета при Президенте РФ по культуре и искусству (с 21.07.2011)

Второй фестиваль «A tutta forza!»
Итальянское выражение «a tutta forza» без перевода вошло в разные языки мира в значении действия максимально эффективного, сконцентрированного в пространстве и времени. В итальянском языке оно означает буквально «в полную силу», «на полную мощность», «во весь дух». На сленге моряков это «Полный вперёд!», у автогонщиков – «Газ до отказу!» Что же значит «a tutta forza» для музыкантов? Творчество с полной самоотдачей, профессиональную зрелость, предельную яркость и глубину художественного высказывания. В фестивале участвуют известные музыканты, обладающие множеством наград, лауреатских регалий и почётных званий, концертирующие по всему миру и передающие свой опыт юным музыкантам. Приобщение к лучшим традициям отечественного исполнительского искусства стало основой их становления и успеха, способности жить в музыке «в полную силу».

Liszt F.Czardas Macabre S224.YT_description:
A screening video I made in late 2012 of Franz Liszt's Csárdás macabre, S.224 (1881-82), which I had previously played for my student recital in Spring 2012.

Liszt wrote three Csárdás pieces in the last decade of his life, titled after the Hungarian folk dance.  Csárdás macabre in particular seems to make reference to the "Danse Macabre" of late Mediaeval art, a subject which already appeared in Romantic works such as Liszt's Totentatz (1849) and Saint-Saëns' Danse Macabre, Op. 40 (1874).

Liszt borrows the four-note motive of the trio sections from one of two proposed sources: the plainchant Dies Irae, or the Hungarian folk song "Ég a kunyhó, ropog a nád."  Perhaps he meant to recall both?  In any case, the work was never published in Liszt's lifetime.  In true spirit to the sly humour of the piece, Liszt wrote over the title page of his manuscript: "May one write or listen to such a thing?"

Felix Mendelssohn Prelude In B Minor Op. 104a No. 2
Performed by Christopher Webb

A very under-rated piece, deserved of much more fame and attention.

The majority of this recording is a single take, though I admit to splicing in order to correct 3 little slips.
I always discourage my students from leaning forward like I naughtily do in this video.
I hope to learn to play without looking so tense in the future.

If you have any suggestions or constructive criticisms, I'd love to read them. I'm fairly sure I am not yet getting the most out of my equipment (audio, visual, or biological).

I hope you enjoy it!

Alexandre Tansman (12 June 1897 – 15 November 1986) was a Polish composer and virtuoso pianist of Jewish origin. He spent his early years in his native Poland, but lived in France for most of his life, being granted French citizenship in 1938. His Polish identity influenced several orchestral and chamber works, such as Rapsodie polonaise and Quatre Danses polonaises, and some guitar works, such as Hommage à Lech Walesa and Hommage à Chopin. His music is often said to be primarily neoclassical, drawing on his Polish Jewish heritage as well as his French musical influences.

1) Allegro deciso
2) Lento
3) Molto vivace
4) Largo. Allegro con moto

[CZ] Alexandre Tansman (polsky Aleksander Tansman, 11. června 1897, Lodž - 15. listopadu 1986, Paříž) byl polský skladatel a klavírní virtuóz žijící ve Francii. Své první hudební vzdělání získal v Lodži. Zde působil v místním symfonickém orchestru pod vedením Tadeusze Mazurkiewicze. Zároveň studoval ve Varšavě hudební teorii u Piotra Rytla, kompozici u Henryka Melcera a hru na klavír u Wojciecha Gawrońského. Na Varšavské univerzitě též studoval právo.

Od roku 1920 až do své smrti žil trvale v Paříži, s přestávkou během druhé světové války, kdy jeho rodina kvůli hrozbě holocaustu žila ve Spojených státech. Do Francie se vrátil v roce 1946.

Alexandre Tansman cestoval jako koncertní pianista po Evropě, Severní Americe i Dálném východě. Zasloužený věhlas získal nejen jako virtuózní klavirista a dirigent, ale i jako skladatel.

Pokud se vám moje tvorba líbí, budu rád, když se přihlásíte k odběru tohoto kanálu, udělíte "palec nahoru" či se vyjádříte v komentářích. Děkuji!

Glinka M.Zhavoronok The lark arr. Balaki.YT_description:
From "East of Melancholy" (Delos Release, 2014) www.delosmusic.com
Perf. by Tara Kamangar www.tarakamangar.net / Dir. by Matthias Heuermann www.form-art.tv
Known as the "Father of Russian Classical Music," composer Mikhail Glinka was raised in Russia with a cosmopolitan upbringing, studying a variety of subjects and languages, including English, German, and Persian. While studying music abroad in Europe as a young man, Glinka saw the opportunity to combine the Russian songs he heard at home with Germanized harmonization. Glinka studied composition in Berlin for five months before returning to Russia at the news of his father's death.

Glinka went on to write two operas based on stories of Russian history which elegantly incorporated elements of Russian folk music. The operas were panned by audiences, whereupon Glinka decided to return to Europe, saying “I don’t want to have anything to do with Russian music- any more than with Russian winters....May I never see the damned country again.” Within less than a year, in 1857, he died in Berlin.

**"The Lark" was originally written for voice and piano by Glinka, and later arranged for piano by his protégé Mily Balakirev. The translated lyrics to the original song are as follows:

Between heaven and earth 
The song spreads 
Sounding ever
Stronger and stronger.

The wind carries the song
To whom it does not know
But knowing that she for whom it is meant
Will recognize from whom it comes.

One cannot see this singer of the fields 
Who sings so loudly
Seeking his mate,
The lark with his ringing song.

Go my song
Song of sweet hope
To one who will remember me
With a secret sigh.

(Poem by Nestor Kukolnik, English translation by Molly Liem)

Scriabin A.Prelude - op 33 no 4 Ab major.YT_description:
Scriabin - Prelude Op. 33 No. 4 in A flat Major - " Ardito, Bellicoso " Played by Tal-Haim Samnon. Part of an Artist Diploma Recital which took place on October 9th at the Jacobs School of Music. Tal-Haim Samnon was born in Tel Aviv in 1986. From the age of six till eighteen he took piano lessons with Mrs. Hanna Shalgi of the Givatayim Music Conservatory. Since then he studied with Prof. Arie Vardi for six years at the Buchman- Mehta school of Music in Tel Aviv University where he did his B.A. In present time he studies with Prof. Evelyne Brancart at the Jacobs School of Music in Indiana University, Bloomington. Tal graduated from the Thelma- Yellin High School for the Performing Arts and served in the Israeli Army as "distinguished musician", enabling him to pursue his musical career uninterruptedly. 
Since the age of seven he has performed at many concerts in Israel and in Europe: Germany, Austria, France, Scotland, Holland, Switzerland and Portugal and more. He often performs for the Israeli "voice of music" channel, both in live broadcasts and in recordings, and has recorded for the Dutch radio as well.
Tal has been awarded the America-Israel Cultural Foundation scholarships since 1998, the "Ronen foundation" scholarships and "Buchman-Heyman foundation" scholarship.
He has appeared with several orchestras as a soloist, such as the Thelma-Yellin Orchestra, the Kibbutzim Orchestra, the Jerusalem Symphony Orchestra, the Israeli Chamber Orchestra, the Rishon Lezion Orchestra and was a soloist at a festive gala concert with Israel Philharmonic Orchestra under Maestro Zubin Mehta, marking the opening of the Buchman Mehta College of Music in Tel-Aviv.
He has taken part in many master classes, including those at Tel Hai with internationally known pianists such as Alexander Korsantia, John O'Connor and Pnina Zaltzman, Victor Derevianko, Leslie Howrad, Peter Tackacs, Jacob Lateiner, Boris Berman, Murray Perahia and more.
He won the Turgeman competition, the Paul Ben Haim competition, the "Highlights", the Ariana Katz, the "Maurice M. Clairmont", the "Young artist", "Lions Israel ", the "Tel Hai International Master Classes Competition" and the Zubin Mehta Piano Competition.

Liszt F.Hungarian Rhapsody No 11 S. 2441.YT_description:
Hungarian Rhapsody No. 11, S.244/11, in A minor, is the eleventh Hungarian Rhapsody by Franz Liszt. He composed a set of 19 piano pieces based on Hungarian folk themes during 1846–1853, and later in 1882 and 1885. 
Liszt also arranged versions for orchestra, piano duet and piano trio.
Some are better known than others, with Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2 being particularly famous. This rhapsody no.11 is sharing similar features to the famous No.2
In their original piano form, the Hungarian Rhapsodies are noted for their difficulty (Liszt was a virtuoso pianist as well as a composer)

Hazel Nguyen began her music education at the age of three. Developing a controlled, prodigious technique, she has been praised for her authority over the most complex technically demanding pieces, the depth of her musical insight and charismatic stage presence. 
With a full scholarship to study at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland, she graduated with a First-Class Bachelor Degree in Joint-Principal Conducting and Piano Performance. At the Royal College of Music, she achieved Master of Music with Distinction in Piano Performance. 
Currently, Hazel is teaching at Rossall School in Lancashire and Sedbergh School in Cumbria, as well as judging competitions and performing worldwide. She is also one of the youngest examiners for ABRSM in the UK.
In addition, Hazel is a recording artist for Tomplay in Switzerland, a transcriber, an arranger and business partner for Musescore UK.
You can find her latest videos here https://www.youtube.com/user/hazel20111993/ 
In the past, Hazel was awarded Worthing Pianist of The Year. At Brighton Springboard Music Festival, she won the Senior Championship, as well as the Senior Concerto Class. As a result, she will be performing with Brighton Orchestra in the next seasons. 
Her virtuosic recording of Beethoven’s Bagatelle op.33 no.5 was played on BBC Radio 3 and made signature for their program In Tune. In Glasgow, producing the best performance of a Mozart Concerto, she was awarded Jock Holden Memorial Trophy. Hazel won the Rosanne Archibald prize for the most promising musician at Blackburn Music Festival and was also a winner at Glasgow Rising Star competition.

Nghệ sĩ piano Hazel Nguyen, tên đầy đủ là Nguyễn Ngọc Trà My, bắt đầu học nhạc từ năm ba tuổi. Kỹ thuật trên phím đàn của cô được cho là xuất sắc. Hazel thường được khen ngợi vì chinh phục thành công những tác phẩm đòi hỏi kỹ thuật phức tạp nhất, chiều sâu âm nhạc sâu lắng nhất, và trên hết là những màn biểu diễn lôi cuốn của cô. 
Với học bổng toàn phần trao tặng bởi Học Viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Scotland năm 2012, cô đã tốt nghiệp chuyên ngành Piano và Chỉ Huy Dàn Nhạc với tấm bằng hạng nhất. Ngay sau đó, Hazel đã tốt nghiệp thạc sĩ chuyên ngành biểu diễn Piano tại Học viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Anh. 
Hiện tại, Hazel đang giảng dạy tại trường Rossall thuộc hạt Lancashire và trường Sedbergh tại hạt Cumbria, Anh Quốc. Cô cũng tham gia các hoạt động biểu diễn và làm giám khảo cho các cuộc thi âm nhạc trong nước và quốc tế. Thêm vào đó, Hazel là một trong những thành viên trẻ nhất của hội đồng chấm thi âm nhạc hoàng gia Anh ABRSM.
Gần đây, cô là nghệ sĩ thu âm cho hãng Tomplay của Thụy Sĩ, và cũng là  một nhà soạn nhạc và phát triển cho ứng dụng Musescore ở Anh.
Bạn có thể tìm thấy những video của Hazel tại https://www.youtube.com/user/hazel20111993/ 
Những năm qua, Hazel được trao giải Nghệ sĩ piano danh giá của năm tại Worthing. Tại Liên hoan âm nhạc Brighton Springboard, cô đã giành giải nhất tại 3 hạng mục khác nhau, cũng như giải nhất cuộc thi Concerto. Cô sẽ biểu diễn cùng Dàn nhạc Brighton trong các mùa diễn tiếp theo. 
Bản thu âm Beethoven Bagatelle op.33/5 của cô đã phát trên BBC Radio 3 và được dùng làm nhạc nền chính cho chương trình In Tune của họ. Tại Glasgow, nhờ màn trình diễn thuyết phục của Mozart Concerto số 12 cung La trưởng, Hazel đã chiến thắng với Cúp tưởng niệm Jock Holden dành cho người chơi Mozart xuất sắc nhất. Cô cũng là người chiến thắng tại cuộc thi Ngôi sao đang lên của Glasgow. Hazel còn giành giải thưởng Rosanne Archibald cho nghệ sĩ triển vọng nhất tại Blackburn Music Festival.

Hassler J.Un poco vivo in D major Op 38.YT_description:
Un Poco Vivo by Johann Wilhelm Hässler performed by Sam Thomas.

Johann Wilhelm Hässler (March 29, 1747 – March 22, 1822), was a German composer, organist and pianist.[1]

Hässler was born in Erfurt. He first studied under his uncle Johann Christian Kittel, who was an organist at Erfurt. His first post was as organist of the local Barfüßerkirche in around 1762. His father died in 1769 and from then on he also managed the family fur business, though he still managed concert tours of Germany in the early 1770s, then in other places in Europe in the 1780s and 1790s. On 15 April 1789 he entered an organ competition with Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart in Dresden during Mozart's Berlin journey. On these tours he also came into contact with Johann Nikolaus Forkel, Johann Adam Hiller, Franz Benda, and Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach. He spent 1790 to 1792 in London and then moved to Saint Petersburg before settling in Moscow in 1794, where he worked as a prominent music teacher and composer. He remained there until his death.
His publications include many keyboard works, including sonatas, fantasies, preludes, and his best known piano work, the Grand Gigue in D minor, Op. 31; as well as a Grand Concert, Op. 50, a cantata, chamber works and songs. One of the most unusual of Hässler's compositions is a cycle of 360 preludes in all keys Op. 47, published in 1817.[citation needed] This massive cycle that lasts for over 95 minutes was premiered in Erfurt by Dmitry Feofanov on September 23, 2012 and in Moscow on September 26, 2012. It was recorded in 2017. (Wiki)

Hazel is an experienced piano teacher and an active concert pianist.
------------------------
Subscribe for more https://www.youtube.com/hazelnguyen Nhớ Theo Dõi để cập nhật những video mới nhất của Hazel nhé!
CONNECT WITH HAZEL NGUYEN ON SOCIAL MEDIA/ TƯƠNG TÁC VỚI HAZEL NGUYỄN TRÊN CÁC KÊNH MXH:
► Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/hazelnguyenpianist/ 
► Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/Hazelnguyenpianist/  
► Free Music Sheets written by Hazel: https://musescore.com/hazelnguyen/  
------------------------
Hazel Nguyen began her music education at the age of three. Developing a controlled, prodigious technique, she has been praised for her authority over the most complex technically demanding pieces, the depth of her musical insight and charismatic stage presence. 
With a full scholarship to study at the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland, she graduated with a First-Class Bachelor Degree in Joint-Principal Conducting and Piano Performance. At the Royal College of Music, she achieved Master of Music with Distinction in Piano Performance. 
Currently, Hazel is teaching at Rossall School in Lancashire and Sedbergh School in Cumbria, as well as judging competitions and performing worldwide. She is also one of the youngest examiners for ABRSM in the UK.
In addition, Hazel is a recording artist for Tomplay in Switzerland, a transcriber, an arranger and business partner for Musescore UK.
You can find her latest videos here https://www.youtube.com/user/hazel20111993/ 
In the past, Hazel was awarded Worthing Pianist of The Year. At Brighton Springboard Music Festival, she won the Senior Championship, as well as the Senior Concerto Class. As a result, she will be performing with Brighton Orchestra in the next seasons. 
Her virtuosic recording of Beethoven’s Bagatelle op.33 no.5 was played on BBC Radio 3 and made signature for their program In Tune. In Glasgow, producing the best performance of a Mozart Concerto, she was awarded Jock Holden Memorial Trophy. Hazel won the Rosanne Archibald prize for the most promising musician at Blackburn Music Festival and was also a winner at Glasgow Rising Star competition. 
------------------------
Nghệ sĩ piano Hazel Nguyen, tên đầy đủ là Nguyễn Ngọc Trà My, bắt đầu học nhạc từ năm ba tuổi. Kỹ thuật trên phím đàn của cô được cho là xuất sắc. Hazel thường được khen ngợi vì chinh phục thành công những tác phẩm đòi hỏi kỹ thuật phức tạp nhất, chiều sâu âm nhạc sâu lắng nhất, và trên hết là những màn biểu diễn lôi cuốn của cô. 
Với học bổng toàn phần trao tặng bởi Học Viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Scotland năm 2012, cô đã tốt nghiệp chuyên ngành Piano và Chỉ Huy Dàn Nhạc với tấm bằng hạng nhất. Ngay sau đó, Hazel đã tốt nghiệp thạc sĩ chuyên ngành biểu diễn Piano tại Học viện âm nhạc hoàng gia Anh. 
Hiện tại, Hazel đang giảng dạy tại trường Rossall thuộc hạt Lancashire và trường Sedbergh tại hạt Cumbria, Anh Quốc. Cô cũng tham gia các hoạt động biểu diễn và làm giám khảo cho các cuộc thi âm nhạc trong nước và quốc tế. Thêm vào đó, Hazel là một trong những thành viên trẻ nhất của hội đồng chấm thi âm nhạc hoàng gia Anh ABRSM.
Gần đây, cô là nghệ sĩ thu âm cho hãng Tomplay của Thụy Sĩ, và cũng là  một nhà soạn nhạc và phát triển cho ứng dụng Musescore ở Anh.
Bạn có thể tìm thấy những video của Hazel tại https://www.youtube.com/user/hazel20111993/ 
Những năm qua, Hazel được trao giải Nghệ sĩ piano danh giá của năm tại Worthing. Tại Liên hoan âm nhạc Brighton Springboard, cô đã giành giải nhất tại 3 hạng mục khác nhau, cũng như giải nhất cuộc thi Concerto. Cô sẽ biểu diễn cùng Dàn nhạc Brighton trong các mùa diễn tiếp theo. 
Bản thu âm Beethoven Bagatelle op.33/5 của cô đã phát trên BBC Radio 3 và được dùng làm nhạc nền chính cho chương trình In Tune của họ. Tại Glasgow, nhờ màn trình diễn thuyết phục của Mozart Concerto số 12 cung La trưởng, Hazel đã chiến thắng với Cúp tưởng niệm Jock Holden dành cho người chơi Mozart xuất sắc nhất. Cô cũng là người chiến thắng tại cuộc thi Ngôi sao đang lên của Glasgow. Hazel còn giành giải thưởng Rosanne Archibald cho nghệ sĩ triển vọng nhất tại Blackburn Music Festival.

Amy Marcy Cheney Beach (September 5, 1867 – December 27, 1944) was an American composer and pianist. She was the first successful American female composer of large-scale art music. Her "Gaelic" Symphony, premiered by the Boston Symphony Orchestra in 1896, was the first symphony composed and published by an American woman. She was one of the first American composers to succeed without the benefit of European training, and one of the most respected and acclaimed American composers of her era. As a pianist, she was acclaimed for concerts she gave featuring her own music in the United States and in Germany.

The name of this study piece says it all. A very fun piece to play, and very satisfying once I managed to really let the melody stand out.

Recorded on 2 August 2017

This recording was made after initially learning the piece. I have not memorized it, hence the need to read from the score while playing. I do not claim that this is the way this piece is to be played, nor do I encourage people to copy what I did. I merely record and post this for keeping track of my own progress as a piano player.

Slonimsky N.Modinha Russo-Brasileira.YT_description:
This piece is by the Russian-born American composer, conductor, and pianist Nicolas Slonimsky who lived from 1894 to 1995.  It is entitled "Modinha Russo-Brasileira", and was composed by him during a trip to Brazil in 1941.  A Modinha is a sad Brazilian song.  In a preface to the piece the composer writes:
"When I visited Brazil in September 1941, I was profoundly impressed by the extraordinary and inexplicable affinity between Brazilian modinhas  and Russian city songs.  I asked myself if it were not possible to compose a piece fusing Russian and Brazilian melodic elements.  This Modinha Russo-Brasileira is the result of my attempt."

I wish to thank my friend Linda in California for finding and sharing this obscure piece with me.  I hope you enjoy it.

Chaminade C.Gigue in C major Op 123 No 6.YT_description:
Cécile Chaminade (1857-1944) was a popular, highly skilled, and prolific French composer and pianist. Her Album des Enfants, Op. 123 (1906) is a delightful collection of character pieces and dances that can serve as excellent pedagogical material for the developing pianist. 

Her music reminds piano students that great art emerges from the human spirit, developed by hard work--irrespective of gender or nationality. Since Chaminade is under-appreciated today, these recordings of her pieces hope to raise awareness of her contributions to the trajectory of Western Art music--especially in the realm of piano pedagogy. Fellow composer Ambroise Thomas complimented the strength of Chaminade’s work: "This is not a woman who composes, but a composer who is a woman." This piece was performed by Chicago-area pianist and teacher, Faith Loewe Lucas, in February, 2020.

Production credits: David Huettner and Anna Friedman. Location: St. John Lutheran Church, Forest Park, IL.

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 414 D major.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in D major K. 414.
00:10 Introduction
01:29 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
Se vi dicessi che la Sonata in Re maggiore K. 414 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi è una “toccata”, potreste benissimo reagire con un “E allora? Ne ha scritte diverse...”, ed avreste comppletamente ragione! Questa, però, è speciale: è una Sonata che cela un segreto, un colpo di scena. Comincia come ogni tipica toccata di Scarlatti: un incedere ritmico inarrestabile anima tutti i trucchi del mestiere che conosce Domenico, salti, note doppie, passi brillanti su e giù per la tastiera che richiedono un tastiersimo atletico. In apertura di seconda parte, però, avviene il genio. Domenico cambia il tono della musica completamente, scrive un episodio dal sapore esotico attraverso il quale possiamo intuire un lontao corteo. Chissà, forse dei dignitari stranieri sono attesi a corte? Questo è un momento davvero ipnotizzante. Poi, ovviamente, l'idea brillante dell'inizio ritorna con prepotenza, e chiude la sonata in un clima di rocambolesca virtuosità dispensata a briglia sciolta. Per me è un gran bel pezzo di musica.
Buon ascolto.

Yared G.Cest le vent Betty.YT_description:
Literally, ' It's the wind, Betty', this is the published piano version of a piece from the soundtrack to the 1986 Jean-Jacques Beineix movie.  The music is by the Lebanese composer Gabriel Yared (1949- ), famous for his music to 'The English Patient', 'The Talented Mr. Ripley' and many others.  In its original scoring, the melody is taken by harmonica over a laid back guitar and percussion accompaniment, and the deliberate accented interruptions in the bass line are taken by (what I think is) a guitar overdrive effect.  In this piano version (which is faithful to the original) the piece comes over to me like an update on the Chopin 'Berceuse'.

Williams C.The dream of Olwen.YT_description:
Charles Williams (real name Isaac Cozerbreit) (1893-1978) was a British conductor and composer of film and light music who took the same professional name as his Polish-born father, who was also in the entertainment business.  This piece - the theme from the British 1947 film 'While I Live' (aka 'The Dream of Olwen') - is one of Williams' best known pieces and was enormously popular in the 1940s and 1950s.  I have used the published solo version (with slight augmentation of the last bar).  The film itself - with its sleepwalking scene, and reincarnation subject matter - made a huge impact on me when I saw it on black-and-white television in the early 1960s.  I was reminded of this in June 2022 when I saw the obituary of the actress Carol Raye (died 18 June 2022) who played the young woman who played the amnesia-suffering pianist in the film.   For more on Charles Williams, see: http://bit.ly/2ulEGeS

Hensel F.Andante espressivo - op 6 no 1.YT_description:
Susan Jane Matthews, piano
Recorded May 6, 2020

As a child, Fanny and her younger brother Felix Mendelssohn played together with the idea of singing piano pieces, Songs without Words or in German, "Lieder ohne Worte."   The opening of Andante espressivo in fact recalls the opening of one of Felix’s "Lied ohne Worte" in the same key, but Fanny’s miniature then traverses some fourteen harmonic areas, revealing her unique compositional spirit. "Andante espressivo" was published in 1847 as the first of Vier Lieder, Opus 6, the fourth of this set the tantalizing "Il saltarello Romano."  This was the last opus published during her lifetime.

Scriabin A.Mazurka - op 3 no 6 C major.YT_description:
Alexander Nikolajewitsch Skrjabin (1871/72 - 1915)

Mazurka No. 6 Scherzando

These Mazurkas (10) are early works and thus show relatively little of the advanced compositional features that began to appear in Scriabin's piano output around the beginning of the twentieth century. Still, while they exhibit the influence of Chopin and Schumann, these Mazurkas divulge the composer's burgeoning musical persona, his characteristic sense of improvisation, and of quirkiness in the flow of the main line. Most are short, lasting about two or three minutes each, with the exception of the six- or seven-minute No. 10.
The perky but elegant Mazurka in B minor No. 1, marked Tempo giusto, with its stately, grand central section, exhibits that quirky but charming Scriabin-esque melodic flow. No. 2 (Allegretto non tanto), in F sharp minor, is rife with modulations in its ebullience and charm. The ensuing Mazurka in G minor (Allegretto) is a melancholy, stormy piece that clearly betrays the influence of Chopin. The E major No. 4 (Moderato) seems to serenely float along one moment, then turn jaunty and playful, if not oafish, the next.
No. 5 (Doloroso), in D sharp minor, is also melancholy and one of the more rewarding offerings in the set. It is Schumann-esque and thematically richer than most of its siblings here, reaching a considerable expressive depth in its generally meditative moods. The C sharp minor No. 6 (Scherzando) is, as its marking indicates, a Scherzo, brilliant and playful in its outer sections -- calling to mind Liszt -- and relatively subdued in its middle panel. The ensuing mazurka (Con passione), in E minor, lives up to the spirit of its marking, with a strong sense of passion and yearning (or is it regret?) in its mostly descending melodic lines.
No. 8 (Con moto), in B flat minor, is elegant and Chopin-esque, and as it progresses, the sense of nostalgia grows, the hints of Chopin turning up in almost every phrase. No. 9, in G sharp minor, bears no tempo marking but is generally played at a moderate pacing. Its mood is melancholy, but often shifts to an agitated expressive manner. The final mazurka (Sotto voce), in the highly unusual key of E flat minor, is, as mentioned above, the longest. It is also the most complex, mixing a sense of the playful and melancholy, and exhibiting snatches of the young composer's later, more individual style, especially in the middle section.

Alexej Outekhin, piano

Gershwin G.Three Preludes No 1.YT_description:
Bản dịch tiếng Việt ở bên dưới.
Three Preludes are short piano pieces by George Gershwin, which were first performed by the composer at the Roosevelt Hotel in New York City in 1926. Each prelude is a well-known example of early-20th-century American classical music, as influenced by jazz.
Gershwin dedicated his Preludes to friend and musical advisor Bill Daly.

The first prelude, in B-flat major, begins with a five-note blues motif; virtually all the melodic material in the piece is based on this theme. Syncopated rhythms based on the Brazilian baião and chords containing flattened sevenths occur throughout; these give the piece a strong jazz feel. Although these sounds are far from adventurous by modern standards, to the audiences of the late 1920s they were almost unheard of.

Mendelssohn F.Capriccio in E major Op 11.YT_description:
Piece: Capriccio, Op. 118 in E Major/e minor 
Composer: F. Mendelssohn 
Pianist: Brittany Buendia 
Date: March 12th, 2017 
Venue: Chapman University's Hall-Musco Conservatory of Music's Salmon Recital 
From the studio of Dr. Janice Park. 

This senior recital was in part of the degree requirements of a bachelors of music in piano performance. 

Program notes: 
According to music editor Steve Schwartz, Mendelssohn was born into a wealthy banking family and was well off, unlike his colleagues J.S. Bach or even Beethoven. Mendelssohn’s parents were supportive of his interests in music and had him take lessons from a prominent teacher of the time, Carl Friedrich Zelter. Zelter encouraged Mendelssohn to follow Bach and Mozart. Mendelssohn began composing from an early age and composed his first masterpiece at age 15 in a style that was largely of his own invention. Works of this period include the Harmoniemusik for band (1824), the Octet (1825), and the Overture to A Midsummer Night's Dream (1826). With these three pieces, he became one of the most important early Romantic composers. His exposure to Bach led to a fondness for learned counterpoint as well as to his conducting the St. Matthew Passion in 1829, which led to Bach’s revival. From this point forward, he began to perform throughout Europe as a conductor and as a pianist to great success (Schwartz). 
 Mendelssohn's music merged the Romantic-era sentiment and lush melodies with the Classical, Mozartean clarity and poise (Schwartz). The Italian word “capriccio” literally translates to whim or “to one’s fancy.” The English word “capricious” is derived from this and can be defined as “impulsive and unpredictable; determined by chance, impulse, or whim.” Mendelssohn’s “Capriccio” begins with a slower, lyrical section that is written with a lush, song-like melody. This is immediately followed by an unprepared, faster (Allegro), more technical section. This sudden and abrupt change in moods can be considered the “whim” element of the “Capriccio.” Moreover, within the “Allegro” section there are moments where he plays with the juxtaposition of loud vs. soft sections in an unprepared manner, solidifying the changing whim of the capriccio.

Chen P.Thunder in Drought Season.YT_description:
The Chinese composer Chen Peixun (1921-2006) was born in Hong Kong and studied composition at the National Conservatory of Music in Shanghai (1939-41). In 1949 he became a founder-member of the Central Conservatory of Music, Beijing, where he taught composition and orchestration. He returned to his native Hong Kong in 1980, teaching at the Baptist College there till his retirement in 1986.

Chen often made use of Cantonese folk tunes in his music. Some of his arrangements of these have become very popular in China, including this "Thunder in Drought Season” (1959).

Bartok B.In Oriental style No 58 from Mi.YT_description:
Béla Bartók's Mikrokosmos (in Hungarian, Mikrokozmosz) Sz. 107, BB 105 consists of 153 progressive piano pieces in six volumes written between 1926 and 1939. The individual pieces progress from very easy and simple beginner études to very difficult advanced technical displays, and are used in modern piano lessons and education. In total, according to Bartók, the piece "appears as a synthesis of all the musical and technical problems which were treated and in some cases only partially solved in the previous piano works." 

Volumes I and II are dedicated to his son Péter, while volumes V and VI are intended as professionally performable concert pieces. Bartók also indicated that these pieces could also be played on other instruments; Huguette Dreyfus for example has recorded pieces from Volumes III through VI on the harpsichord. And there are transcription made as methods used for learning for other instruments, such as the harp and the guitar. 

In 1940, shortly before they emigrated to the United States, he arranged seven of the pieces for two pianos, to provide additional repertoire for himself and his wife Ditta Pásztory-Bartók to play in concert.

All of the six volumes progress in difficulty, namely:

Volumes I and II: Pieces 1–36 and 37–66, beginner level
Volumes III and IV: Pieces 67–96 and 97–121, moderate to advanced level
Volumes V and VI: 122–139 and 140–153, professional level

(Information with the help of Wikipedia)

These pieces are used in some conservatoires as fundamental learning material, and together with Bach, I believe they cover a vast range a pianistic techniques indispensable to the pianist. 

As compositional works, I believe these pieces to be made with excellent craftsmanship, and a great source of techniques and theoretical materials essential to the composer of the 21st Century.

Morning is the 4th of 8 pieces that make up Opus 43 by the Russian composer Reinhold Gliere.  Gliere lived from 1875 to 1956 and is best known for his symphonic works, but he also wrote some charming piano pieces such as this delightful miniature.

1.  Prelude
2.  Prayer
3.  Mazurka
4.  Morning
5.  Evening
6.  Rondo

"Por una Cabeza" is a tango song written in 1935 with music by Carlos Gardel and lyrics by Alfredo Le Pera. It is featured in a famous tango scene in Martin Brest's film Scent of a Woman (1992), in the opening scene of Steven Spielberg's Schindler's List (1993) and in James Cameron's True Lies (1994)

The name is a Spanish horse-racing phrase meaning "by a head", which refers to a horse winning a race narrowly - by just the length of its head. The lyrics speak of a compulsive horse-track gambler who compares his addiction for horses with his attraction to women.

Carlos Gardel (born Charles Romuald Gardès; 11 December 1890 – 24 June 1935) was a French Argentine singer, songwriter, composer and actor, and the most prominent figure in the history of tango. Gardel's baritone voice and the dramatic phrasing of his lyrics made miniature masterpieces of his hundreds of three-minute tango recordings. Together with lyricist and long-time collaborator Alfredo Le Pera, Gardel wrote several classic tangos.

Gardel died in an airplane crash at the height of his career, becoming an archetypal tragic hero mourned throughout Latin America. For many, Gardel embodies the soul of the tango style. He is commonly referred to as "Carlitos", "El Zorzal" (The [Song] Thrush), "The King of Tango", "El Mago" (The Wizard), "El Morocho del Abasto" (The Brunette boy from Abasto), and ironically "El Mudo" (The Mute).

Alfredo Le Pera was an Argentine, born in Brazil, son of Italian immigrants. Le Pera and Gardel died in an airplane crash in Medellín, on Monday, June 24, 1935.

The starting phrase in the B section may be inspired by Mozart's Rondo for violin and orchestra in C major, K. 373.

The song was originally composed in A major. It was thereafter adapted to the violin and the piano sometimes in A major, sometimes in G major.

The French composer, pianist and organist Alexandre-Pierre-François Boëly (1785-1856) was largely self-taught as a composer, although he came from a musical family.  In his youth he studied the piano works of Clementi and Bach, and this grounding can be seen in the sober, intellectual style of his music, which has affinities with his near-contemporary JB. Cramer.  His works are mainly small-scale collections for piano, organ and chamber ensembles, although he did write some liturgical vocal works and a (lost) symphony.  This piece is the last in an untitled set of twelve pieces, and, though written around 1830, was first published in Fétis' 'Revue Musicale' in 1833.

Kabalevsky Op. 27 no. 10 Clowning
The trick here is to keep your hands out of one another's way.  The best way to achieve this is to keep your left hand further in from the right hand.  Make sure to use a strict staccato - otherwise you'll find the key still down when the right hand needs it. Use care when engaging and releasing the una corda pedal as the keyboard will shift slightly.

Czerny C.Easy exercises Op 139 No 86.YT_description:
こんにちは！

今日は、一気に70曲、ツェルニー100番の残りを載せます！！（撮影と編集、た、た、大変だった…）
通知がとんでもないことになってしまいますが、今日だけご容赦いただけたら幸いです。
たくさんの方からずっとリクエストいただいていたにも関わらず、遅くなってしまいました…！
この動画が少しでも皆様の練習のお役に立てたら嬉しいです😄


⭐ツェルニー100番について

ツェルニー100番においてはほぼペダルは使わず、指でのレガートを意識しています。
それは小さい頃から必ず意識したほうが良いことです。
この練習曲集において、速く適当に弾いてしまうことは何よりも危険です。とにかくゆっくり丁寧に、自分の音を聞きながら弾くことを絶対に推奨します（我が生徒たちにも口酸っぱく言っていることです）

私自身、今回演奏する際に何よりも重視したのは丁寧さです。実は速く弾くことよりもゆっくり弾くことのほうが難しかったりします。ぜひ皆様も、ゆっくり丁寧に自分の音を聞きながら練習してみてくださいね😉🎵

ーーーー

小さい頃から大好きだったツェルニー。
今では教える立場となり、「教えるために弾く」場面が増え、その魅力を再認識する日々を送っていました。
嫌いな方も多いツェルニーですが、私は先生の演奏やピアニストのCDに憧れ、こんな風に弾けるようになりたい…！と、一生懸命に練習していた気がします。今の時代非常に便利な動画でツェルニーを見て、楽しく練習してもらえたら。ツェルニーのことを大好きになってもらえたら。そんな気持ちを込めて、演奏いたしました。

手首や指の使い方が一番伝わりやすいアングルで撮ったつもりでおります。音だけでなく、フィジカルな面での使い方も是非、参考にしていただければ嬉しいです。


＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝＝

このチャンネルでは、主にピアノ学習中に必ず通るエチュードやバッハを載せています🌸

The etudes from Heller Op. 45, 46 and 47 are an excellent source of repertoire from which teachers may choose pieces to develop their intermediate-level students sense of the nineteenth-century style, technical skills and musical sensitivity (L.M. Kiefer).

Bacharach B.Raindrops keep falling on my.YT_description:
--TEACHER DEMO--
This classic song from 1969 originally made its appearance in the movie "Butch Cassidy & the Sundance Kid" where it won an Academy Award for Best Original Song. B.J. Thomas did the original recording which I am partial to, but many other vocal artists have recorded it since then. Billboard Magazine ranked this song at number 15 in its Top 50 Movie Songs of All Time in 2014, and it was also inducted into the 2014 Grammy Hall of Fame. This song has been used in many movies and TV shows including:  Spy Hard, Spiderman 2, The In-Laws, Forrest Gump, The Simpsons, and many others. 

The lyrics were composed by Hal David and the music by Burt Bacharach, who has won many awards through the years for his creative talent. This masterful arrangement for piano is by Mark Hayes.  Mark Hayes is one of my favorite arrangers of all time.  He specializes in Sacred music, but has also done a wonderful collection of "Film Classics" for advanced piano in the Alfred's Popular Performer Series. --Norma

Confrey Z.Dizzy Fingers.YT_description:
Edward Elzear ('Zez') Confrey (1895-1971) was an American popular composer and maker of piano rolls, whose novelty rags, mood pieces, popular songs etc. in some ways paralleled the output of the British composer Billy Mayerl.  Both composers were involved in teaching pianists to play 'modern' popular music.  'Dizzy Fingers'  is one of his best-known solos, and has been on the Trinity Guildhall Grade 8 piano exam syllabus.  I have included all repeats in my CPP/Belwin edition (and I note that TG ask tor them to be played in the exam).  It is a monster of a piece for doing one's own page turns, and I only managed this performance by identifying repeated passages reprinted in full over six pages.  Maybe the Alfred edition recommended by TG handles it better!

Scarlatti D.Sonata in C major K 157.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in C major K. 157.
00:10 Introduction
02:13 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
Il mio amico Roberto Zecchini è un uomo dai tanti talenti. Non solo è uno dei più importanti editori di musica in questo Paese, ma è anche un clarinettista e fenomenale collezionista di dischi. Ha preso l'abitudine di pubblicare sui suoi social le copertine di alcuni suoi rarissimi LP, invitando i suoi numerosi amici ad intavolare spesso furiose ma sempre interessantissime discussioni su questioni di storia, compositori, interpreti, stili, e via discorrendo. Lui non lo sa, ma ultimamente mi ha ispirato. Ha pubblicato la copertina di un album devoto alla musica rinascimentale per flauto dolce, e quello mi ha fatto venire in mente che uno dei notevoli talenti di Domenico era proprio quello di ripensare antiche forme musicali in un idioma ammodernato. La sua Sonata in Do maggiore K. 157 che presenteremo oggi è un Saltarello, ossia una danza medievale del centro Italia in tempo ternario veloce. Oramai sappiamo bene che quando Domenico scrive qualcosa in tempo ternario veloce da qualche parte ci sono i fuochi d'artificio, e questa Sonata non fa eccezione: Domenico usa l'idea del Saltarello per scrivere un magnifico esemplare di tessitura tastieristica, e fra le meraviglie che si trovano in questa musica ci sono i poliritmi, modulazioni ardite e, nella seconda parte, perfino accenni ad un drammatico lirismo. Soprattutto, però, Domenico chiude entrambe le parti del pezzo con un'esplosione di gioia che pare gridare al mondo “Viva la Musica!”. Ed io sono convinto che Roberto Zecchini sia d'accordo con noi quando gridiamo “Viva le Musica”! 
Buon ascolto.
Scarlatti D.Sonata in C major K 157.YT_title: SCARLATTI / ALL SONATAS #453: Sonata in C major K. 157

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 526 C minor.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in c minor K. 526.
00:10 Introduction
03:47 Sonata 
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
Uno dei benefici di questo progetto è la possibilità di leggere le vivaci discussioni nelle quali alcuni ascoltatori si producono. Le trovo estremamente istruttive, perché nessuno, in musica, è depositario della verità. Possiamo vedere lo stesso lavoro da punti di vista diametralmente opposti, ed essere pur sempre nel giusto, ed in questo, la musica è facilmente la più democratica di tutte le arti. Ad esempio, qualche giorno fa uno dei mei più assidui commentatori, il Signor Giacobbe Nevio Zanivan, ha argomentato che la classificazione della musica in periodi storici (Barocco, Classico, Romantico eccetera) è poco più d'una tassonomia, forse un attrezzo didattico. Ci ho pensato un paio di giorni, e mi senti di concordare con lui. Di certo, conosco pezzi di musica “romantica” che sembrano barocchi, e pezzi “barocchi” che paiono romantici (e Domenico ce ne ha già dato ampia dimostrazione). Quando si interpreta la musica un minimo di analisi è fondamentale, ma è difficile dosarla. Se si analizza troppo poco si è superficiali, ma se si analizza troppo si corre il rischio di soffocare la musica con le nozioni e si verifica quello che chiamo “paralisi da analisi”. Ci vuole esperienza per sapere quando è arrivato il momento di smettere. Naturalmente, tutto questo scompare quando siamo di fronte ad un capolavoro, e la Sonata in do minore K. 526 di Domenico Scarlatti è un grande capolavoro. Si tratta di una fantasia contrappuntistica che comincia in unto stile molto austero e severo. La natura della scrittura polifonica è esponenziale: prima una voce, poi due, poi tre, e la musica crea l'impressione di un qualcosa che cresce, cresce, cresce... Questo è esattamente quel che fa Domenico per tutta la prima pagina del pezzo, finché ad un certo punto si ritrova in capo al mondo e deve scendere, deve tornare giù. Lui è un genio, sicché scrive un passaggio di bellezza indicibile, una di quelle frasi che ti spezzano il cuore, e riporta la musica ad un livello più tranquillo con il quale chiude la prima parte della Sonata. All'esordio della seconda parte, si trova di nuovo una grande apertura realizzata con scale a tutta tastiera che sfociano in un passaggio mirabolante di trilli doppi che sembrano grida. Devo dire che il tono di tutta la Sonata è di cupa disperazione, e trilli doppi, forse, sono il modo in cui Domenico sottolinea proprio l'aspetto più tragico e disperato di questa musica. Poco dopo ritorna il bellissimo passaggio della prima parte, ma questa volta è scritto in maniera più snella e lineare perché Domenico deve finire la Sonata. Lo fa con una delle sue trovate: una figura in terzine, accompagnata da note molto gravi alla mano sinistra che sembrano lugubri rintocchi di campane, magari in occasione d'un funerale. Questa Sonata è un pezzo di musica molto vivido, non particolarmente impegnativo tecnicamente, ma musicalmente affine ad un campo minato. Nella mia opinione, questo è il lavoro di un autentico Grande Maestro.
Buon ascolto.

Bartok B.Canon (No 29) from For Children.PS_title: Canon (No 29) from For Children 2 BB 53 Sz 42
Bartok B.Canon (No 29) from For Children.YT_description:
Here is my new recording, made last weekend, of  Bartók's educational set For Children. The colorful Hungarian title "A Gyermekeknek" somehow always amuses me. The pieces were penned down in 1908/09, but Bartók revised the set in 1945, towards the end of his life, leaving out 6 pieces and slightly altering others. It is this final version that I play here.

The two books are quite different in character. I marginally prefer 
Book I, based on Hungarian Folk Tunes. These are more ebullient, the colors brighter, than those in Book II, based on Slovak Folk Tunes, which are generally darker and more introspective, at times 
reminiscent of Janacek (as they ought to be, being Slovak). 

Both books contain a wealth of great music, and certainly not all of the pieces seen suitable for children - unless they have advanced technique and musicality. I hope my cycle can be enjoyed despite a couple of small read errors (which, obviously and  irritatingly, I only noticed during video preparation).

Schubert F.Sonata Op. Post. in A major D.PS_title: Sonata Op. Post. in A major D 959 - mvt 3 Scherzo and Trio
Schubert F.Sonata Op. Post. in A major D.YT_description:
Does it seem to you that the world has gone mad? Wars, bombings, killings, hate....
I can offer but a little remedy, an escape rather. Music equivalent of "slow TV", something created not to excite our overdriven nerves, but to soothe, to lull, to put in ultimate trance, to make the time stand still and the troubles of outside world fade away, if only for a few minutes. 
Nobody has done it better than my beloved Franz Schubert. 
There is a famous quip about two musicians arguing over the merits ( or weaknesses) of Schubert late piano sonatas, one describing the unusual time span of the pieces as "the heavenly lengths", another - replying "they aren't that  heavenly, they are just plain LENGTHS".
Yes, Schubert is unique in a sense that he's dispensed not only with customary time restrains established by the need to keep the listener "interested", but also with the medley of rather theatrical "action heroes" prerequisite for a virtuoso performer to feel adequate :) His music is not about heroes and villains, gods and devils.
His music is about you and I, about regular people living their lives, loving, longing, suffering, dying....all without the world taking notice and without the headlines.That's the real charm and beguiling spell of his music - this is about us, the regular human beings, whom he understood better than any other composer. 
You might not be able to fully enjoy this piece from the first try, or if you have your thoughts wondering around, thinking of million little things, looking for easy gratification of virtuoso fingerwork and thunderous chords. 
You will enjoy it if you allow yourself to surrender to this music, to its flow, as slow, smooth and spellbinding asthenia waters of mythical river Lethe, the river of forgetfulness and oblivion.

"J'ai trop vu, 
trop senti, 
trop aimé dans ma vie; 
Je viens chercher vivant le calme du Léthé."

"I have seen too much, 
felt too much, 
loved too much in my life;

I come to seek, still living,
the calm of Lethe."

A.de Lamartine

Friedrich Burgmüller- Fileuse op.109 n.18
Fausto Bongelli, piano
Friedrich Burgmüller, in Paris known under the French form of his name, Frédéric, was born in Regensburg in 1806, the son of the composer, pianist and music teacher Johann August Franz Burgmüller, and elder brother of the composer, conductor and pianist Norbert Burgmüller. Friedrich Burgmüller was taught by his father. After the latter’s death in 1824 he followed him as director of music in Düsseldorf, teaching music in Mühlhausen and as a cellist in Basel. In 1832 he settled in Paris, where he won a considerable reputation as a piano teacher, and internationally as a composer of salon pieces and studies. He did much to promote the work of his brother Norbert, four years his junior, whose career had been cut short by his sudden death at the spa in Aachen in 1836. Friedrich Burgmüller’s activities brought continued success in Paris. Many of his compositions proved successful among amateurs, for whom his pieces offered limited technical challenges, coupled with the satisfaction of musical interest. His Études (‘Studies’) have continued to provide a basis for piano teaching and the development of technical proficiency.

Scarlatti D.Sonata in F major K 317.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in F major K. 317.
00:10 Introduction
01:48 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
Oggi è di nuovo “casa dolce casa”: sono nel mio studio, con il mio vecchio Steinway, ove molti mesi fa cominciò questa grande avventura, e in un certo senso è tempo di decisioni. Questa, accanto a me, è l'edizione curata da Kenneth Gilbert delle 556 Sonate di Scarlatti, tutti gli undici volumi; ora che mancano più o meno sessanta Sonate alle fine del progetto, mentre esaurisco le Sonate che essi contengono alcuni di questi volumi si trasferiranno da questa pila, la quale di solito alberga dietro di me, alla libreria qui accanto. Ho deciso che il primo trasloco toccherà a questo, il Volume Settimo, che contiene la bellissima Sonata in Fa maggiore K. 317 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi. Alla fine di questo episodio, non ci saranno più Sonate da registrare in questo volume. Questa Sonata è particolarmente accattivante: si tratta di un moto perpetuo camuffato da arabesco, una lunga ed ininterrotta figura sinuosa che passa costantemente dalla mano destra alla sinistra e viceversa, in una impressionante dimostrazione di sofisticazione digitale. Quel che stupisce maggiormente, però, è la miriade di permutazioni alle quali Domenico assoggetta l'armonia del pezzo: agendo in modo molto discreto ma decisivo, ci dà quasi l'impressione di osservare un disegno al nero di seppia, in chiaroscuro. È un pezzo di musica di classe monumentale, con il quale diciamo arrivederci al nostro caro Volume Settimo.
Buon ascolto.

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 446 F major.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in F major K. 446 “Pastorale”.
00:10 Introduction
02:15 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La Sonata in Fa maggiore K. 446 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi è fra le più famose, ed è anche una delle pochissime che recano un titolo specifico: Pastorale. Diversi studiosi la considerano compagna della Sonata nello stesso tono K. 445 che presentammo ieri, e forse hanno ragione, specialmente se consideriamo quella brillantissima Toccata come preludio o introduzione alla più riflessiva Pastorale. Praticamente ogni musicista che io conosca esegue questo pezzo in modo molto lirico. Anche il grande Gyorgy Cziffra, del quale ne esiste una esecuzione anche qui su Youtube che, se ne avrete il tempo e la voglia, vale ben la pena di ascoltare: il Maestro suona magnificamente! Personalmente, però, ho un piccolo problema con questo approccio. Accanto al titolo di Pastorale, Domenico ci dà come indicazione di tempo “Allegrissimo”! Ora, è davvero avventuroso cercare di conciliare l'idea popolare di una “pastorale”, di solo un pezzo calmo e riflessivo, con un “Allegrissimo” di Scarlatti. Qui in Italia, soprattutto durante la stagione del Natale, i pastori scendevano dalle montagne per celebrare le festività con un po'di musica allegra, la quale tradizionalmente veniva fatta con cornamuse e pifferi, e vi assicuro che questi due strumenti non solo possono fare musica vivace, ma anche un gran baccano. Ecco che se suoniamo questa Sonata “Allegrissimo”, come chiede Domenico, il pezzo assume una veste totalmente diversa: si lascia dietro ogni traccia di malinconia e pensosità, e diventa una gioiosa celebrazione: quella che qui chiamiamo “pifferata”.
Buon ascolto.

The form of Suite was very popular in baroque. It brings together dances from diferrent parts of Europe making it one integrated whole. There are four dances that originally form the core of the baroque suite: German Allemande, French Courante, Spanish Sarabande and Enligh Gigue. Additionally the Suite could be (and usually was) extended by other dances: Menuet, Passapied or even Polonaise. Bach wrote his six French Suites in year 1722-25 and they were originally designed to be played on a harpsichord. Bach himself considered the Suites as a bridge between the Inventions and Das Wohltemperierte Klavier. The title ‘French’ was not given by the composer but by the society to differentiate the French Suites from the previously written English Suites. Funny enough, they are, however, written in an Italian manner.
There is no surviving manuscript of these Suites, therefore the execution of the ornaments can be a very exciting and inspiring challenge for the performer. The third Suite in B minor is one of the most frequently played ones. It consists of Allemande, Courante, Sarabande, Anglaise (previously named as Gavotte), Menuet, Trio and Gigue.

Scarlatti D.Sonata in A major K. 369.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in A major K. 369.
00:10 Introduction
01:43 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La Sonata in La maggiore K. 369 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi è uno dei grandi lavori che popolano la parte mediana del catalogo assemblato dal Signor Kirkpatrick. Comincia in modo bellissimo, con lunghe catene di note perlacee che incorniciano una melodia quasi pastorale, ed è davvero stupefacente il modo in cui Domenico riesce a creare un'atmosfera così eterogenea in così poche battute di musica. Questa, però, non è altro che l'introduzione. C'è un passo cadenzale, e poi la musica si ferma del tutto. Quel che accade dopo, mi pare come un “flashback” cinematografico. Qui in Toscana, quando ero bambino, giocavamo spesso a chi riuscisse a saltare più in là degli altri. Domenico comincia da un Mi, lo ripete varie volte, e poi comincia ad allontanarsi da esso con salti crescenti: prima una Quarta, poi una Sesta, poi un' Ottava e via via incrementando la distanza, proprio come facevamo noialtri da bambini, fino a che raggiunge il salto di due ottave. Lo reitera tre o quattro volte, ed a questo punto la Sonata si rivela per quel che è: un grande, meraviglioso Fandango! Da qui in avanti, il pezzo si dipana in una folle corsa verso la fine, in un'opera nella quale la virtuosità strumentale procede mano nella mano con il lirismo per la creazione di un capolavoro musicale. Come sempre, è un grande privilegio, per me, potervelo presentare.
Buon ascolto.
Scarlatti D.Sonata in A major K. 369.YT_title: SCARLATTI / ALL SONATAS #438: Sonata in A major K. 369

Bartok B.Revelry (No 22) from For Childr.YT_description:
Here is my new recording, made last weekend, of  Bartók's educational set For Children. The colorful Hungarian title "A Gyermekeknek" somehow always amuses me. The pieces were penned down in 1908/09, but Bartók revised the set in 1945, towards the end of his life, leaving out 6 pieces and slightly altering others. It is this final version that I play here.

The two books are quite different in character. I marginally prefer 
Book I, based on Hungarian Folk Tunes. These are more ebullient, the colors brighter, than those in Book II, based on Slovak Folk Tunes, which are generally darker and more introspective, at times 
reminiscent of Janacek (as they ought to be, being Slovak). 

Both books contain a wealth of great music, and certainly not all of the pieces seen suitable for children - unless they have advanced technique and musicality. I hope my cycle can be enjoyed despite a couple of small read errors (which, obviously and  irritatingly, I only noticed during video preparation).

This 1948 standard by Sonny Burke (1914-80) - with lyrics by Paul Francis Webster - has been recorded by Ella Fitzgerald, Peggy Lee and Sarah Vaughan, amongst many others.  This piano arrangement appeared in the Wise Publications 'Popular Piano Solos' series, and has recently been revived by ABRSM, which has included it in its 2011-12 Grade 7 piano syllabus.  I have not seen their reprint, but would be interested to know if the E natural in the top chord of the second group of triplet crotchets in bar 8 has been changed to a D.  I play it as written, because the same appears in the second appearance of the phrase (but not the third), and I cannot tell if it is a misprint.

Castro R.Nostalgie Op. 44.YT_description:
Note the composer of this piece is nothing to do with the eminent present day Brazilian pianist, Ricardo Castro.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ricardo Castro (1864-1907) was one of the first internationally-prominent Mexican composers.  He studied at the Conservatorio Nacional de Música de México and later toured the USA as a concert pianist.  He visited Europe in the early 1900s to give masterclasses, but died of pneumonia not long after his return to Mexico, having just been appointed director of music at the conservatory.  This beautiful piece was published posthumously in 1908.  It reminds me a little of works of the period from the French 'flute school' (Gaubert, Taffanel etc.) but has a definite Latin flavour.  NB the published score is slightly ambiguous around 2:04 as to whether A's should be sharp or natural, and I may have misinterpreted it - but you are unlikely to notice unless you know the score very well!

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 530 E major.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in E major K. 530.
00:10 Introduction
01:19 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La Sonata in Mi maggiore K 530 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi è una bellissima toccata, e comincia proprio come una tipica toccata di Scarlatti: passi brillantissimi in un ambito musicale fondamentalmente gioioso. Tuttavia, non si tratta di mero virtuosismo strumentale: questo è un pezzo di musica serio. Poco dopo l'inizio, Domenico modula nel tono minore e scrive un paio di passi dal tipico carattere di cantabilità napoletana, e così facendo crea un incredibile contrasto drammatico. Nella seconda parte della Sonata Domenico espande l'idea napoletana, modula in continuazione e si spinge piuttosto lontano dal tono di Mi maggiore. Quando finalmente vi ritorna, chiude la Sonata nello stesso clima di gioia con cui l'aveva iniziata. Questa è squisita maestria, applicata ad una sincera e notevole ispirazione.
Buon ascolto.
Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 530 E major.YT_title: SCARLATTI / ALL SONATAS #388: Sonata in E major K. 530

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 409 B minor.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in b minor K. 409-
00:10 Introduction
01:46 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La Sonata in si minore K. 409 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi è uno di quei pezzi che ben possono ambire al titolo di “musica folle”; mi fa pensare a quelle raganelle che si trovano nella foresta Amazzonica, e che coi loro colori sgargianti dicono ai predatori “Lasciami stare: sono velenosa!”. Ecco, l'ignaro interprete che si decida a leggere questa musica si trova davanti a un pezzo scritto in tre ottavi, con l'indicazione “Allegro”, e pieno di salti pazzeschi alla mano sinistra sin dalla prima battuta. Dopo un esame un po' più approfondito, ci rendiamo conto che questa musica è in odogre di tarantella, e secondo me è la trascrizione di un'improvvisazione sopra l'idea di una tarantella, specialmente perché dopo una serie di funambolismi nella prima parte, Domenico apre la seconda parte del pezzo con dei piccoli accordi arpeggiati su una basa armonica quasi statica L'effetto è ipnotico: questo è un momento di eccezionale bellezza, che per una volta rimane, sospeso nell'aria, per quasi tutta la seconda parte della Sonata. Quando Domenico ritrova il tema dell'inizio, infatti, la Sonata giunge al termine bruscamente e con inesorabile decisione.
Secondo me è un gran bel pezzo di musica.
Buon ascolto.

Scarlatti D.Sonata in F major K 367.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in F major K. 367.
00:10 Introduction
01:45 Sonata 
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
Leggendo le Sonate di Domenico Scarlatti non è difficile imbattersi in passaggi strabilianti per le  più svariate ragioni: spesso è la loro difficoltà infernale a saltare all'occhio, altre volte la bizzarra fantasia, ed altre ancora la purezza di proporzioni e simmetria. Una simile occasione si incontra quando leggiamo la Sonata in Fa maggiore K. 367 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi. Poco dopo l'inizio, si incontra un passo così (accenna alla partitura), fatto di scale in moto contrario. È scritto in modo bellissimo, ed è anche molto bello da ascoltare, direi quasi scioccante. Ma è anche l'ennesima dimostrazione dell'incredibile maliziosità di Domenico. Le scale, come sappiamo, son fatte di sette note. Queste sono undici! Pensateci un attimo: il suonatore ha dieci dita, e Domenico si dev'essere divertito un sacco a scriverne una di più! Questo dettaglio tecnico, ad ogni modo, accade nel mezzo di un bel pezzo di musica: la Sonata è una Jota, una danza spagnola, ed è un crogiolo di grandi idee; Domenico inventa una serie di trucchi ingegnosi in questo piccolo pezzo, ma quando li mettiamo insieme scopriamo che ammontano ad un meraviglioso pezzo di musica.
Buon ascolto.
Scarlatti D.Sonata in F major K 367.YT_title: SCARLATTI / ALL SONATAS #425: Sonata in F major K. 367

John Ireland (1879-1962), was one of the leading British composers for piano of the 20th century.  'The Holy Boy' is perhaps his best-known work. Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 516 D minor.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in d minor K. 516.
00:10 Introduction
02:05 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La Sonata in re minore K. 516 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi è un meraviglioso pezzo di musica che racconta la storia di due realtà diverse. Da una parte c'è la musica stessa, dal carattere molto spagnoleggiante, che descrive una scena rustica, forse in una taverna in Spagna ove si sta per ballare il flamenco. Dall'altra parte, invece, c'è uno dei più grandi tastieristi che la storia ricordi, e che qui sfodera quel tipo di scrittura che pare avere il beneficio d'un intervento divino. La Sonata è fra le più complesse di Domenico, scritta in maniera molto densa, accordale, piena di ornamenti, e, di conseguenza, piuttosto impegnativa da suonare. Ora, l'eredità dei grandi studiosi di Scarlatti, Kirkpatrick prima e Sheveloff poi, vorrebbe che eseguissimo molte di queste Sonate a coppie e quindi, molto spesso, questa Sonata K. 516 viene presentata come preludio alla Sonata nello stesso tono K. 517 che abbiamo presentato qualche giorno fa. Quella è una Sonata molto veloce, e siccome gli interpreti sono sempre a caccia di contrasti, accade che spesso questa K. 516 venga eseguita molto lentamente. Ma il pezzo reca l'indicazione di “Allegretto”. Uno dei benefici del mio progetto è che non do concerti: semplicemente presento ogni sonata cercando di sottolinearne le proprie peculiarità. Vi dico questo perché sono convinto che il carattere di questa musica trovi giovamento da un'esecuzione più vivace del solito. Sia come sia, di una cosa sono certo: questo è un capolavoro.
Buon ascolto.

Grovlez G.Berceuse de la poupee No 2 in.YT_description:
I have always loved this endearing suite by Gabriel Grovlez, a composer about whom I could find little information and only some very sketchy photos. It seems clear that Grovlez was under the spell of Debussy, and I'm pretty sure he must have known that composer's Children's Corner, on which some of these items seem to be modeled. Nonetheless I do not find this derivative music. These pieces, often used in grade exams, are charming, heartfelt, and well-wrought. 

Grovlez wrote a dozen or so other piano works but this is the only one you ever hear. I am intrigued by his Two Etudes of Transcendental Difficulty, but they look so absolutely fiendish that I won't even think of trying them.

I recorded L'Almanach aux Images on Jun 18, 2011. They're not perfect but I hope I have caught(some of) their charm.

Scriabin A.Mazurka - op 3 no 1 B minor.YT_description:
Alexander Nikolajewitsch Skrjabin (1871/72 - 1915)

Mazurka No. 1 Tempo guisto

These Mazurkas (10) are early works and thus show relatively little of the advanced compositional features that began to appear in Scriabin's piano output around the beginning of the twentieth century. Still, while they exhibit the influence of Chopin and Schumann, these Mazurkas divulge the composer's burgeoning musical persona, his characteristic sense of improvisation, and of quirkiness in the flow of the main line. Most are short, lasting about two or three minutes each, with the exception of the six- or seven-minute No. 10.
The perky but elegant Mazurka in B minor No. 1, marked Tempo giusto, with its stately, grand central section, exhibits that quirky but charming Scriabin-esque melodic flow. No. 2 (Allegretto non tanto), in F sharp minor, is rife with modulations in its ebullience and charm. The ensuing Mazurka in G minor (Allegretto) is a melancholy, stormy piece that clearly betrays the influence of Chopin. The E major No. 4 (Moderato) seems to serenely float along one moment, then turn jaunty and playful, if not oafish, the next.
No. 5 (Doloroso), in D sharp minor, is also melancholy and one of the more rewarding offerings in the set. It is Schumann-esque and thematically richer than most of its siblings here, reaching a considerable expressive depth in its generally meditative moods. The C sharp minor No. 6 (Scherzando) is, as its marking indicates, a Scherzo, brilliant and playful in its outer sections -- calling to mind Liszt -- and relatively subdued in its middle panel. The ensuing mazurka (Con passione), in E minor, lives up to the spirit of its marking, with a strong sense of passion and yearning (or is it regret?) in its mostly descending melodic lines.
No. 8 (Con moto), in B flat minor, is elegant and Chopin-esque, and as it progresses, the sense of nostalgia grows, the hints of Chopin turning up in almost every phrase. No. 9, in G sharp minor, bears no tempo marking but is generally played at a moderate pacing. Its mood is melancholy, but often shifts to an agitated expressive manner. The final mazurka (Sotto voce), in the highly unusual key of E flat minor, is, as mentioned above, the longest. It is also the most complex, mixing a sense of the playful and melancholy, and exhibiting snatches of the young composer's later, more individual style, especially in the middle section.

I have always loved this endearing suite by Gabriel Grovlez, a composer about whom I could find little information and only some very sketchy photos. Grovlez wrote a dozen or so other piano works but this is the only one you ever hear. I am intrigued by his Two Etudes of Transcendental Difficulty, but they look so absolutely fiendish that I won't even think of trying them.

Mikrokosmos was originally designed as a collection of pieces for the beginning pianist, but over time it took on grander proportions, comprising 153 individual pieces that spanned the range of technical difficulty. Dividing into six volumes, it begins with pieces for beginners and progresses to those that challenge even the most accomplished pianist. That Mikrokosmos has become a viable progressive method is demonstrated by its ubiquity in the repertories of modern piano students, but its reputation rests on more than its technical and pedagogical applications; Bartók's work represents a varied and finely crafted catalog of twentieth century musical idioms. In Bartók's own words, it "appears as a synthesis of all the musical and technical problems which were treated and in some case only partially solved in the previous piano works." Perhaps chief among these musical problems was Bartók's attempted synthesis of Eastern and Western European musical traditions, particularly Eastern folk music with the Germanic tradition (as represented by Bach and Beethoven) and with the progressive harmonies of Claude Debussy. 

The first 66 pieces in Mikrokosmos (Vols. 1 and 2) are dedicated to Bartók's son, Peter, for whose use they were originally intended. Many of these pieces are technical exercises, useful for developing finger and hand independence, as well as hand span; however, they are also of interest for their musical language. Hungarian folk tunes, pentatonic, whole-tone and modal harmonies, as well as more adventurous octatonic chromatic scales all form the basis for these short pieces. 

Volumes 3 and 4 make up numbers 67 through 121. These pieces display increased harmonic complexity and technical demands. Bartók employs more polymodes (the use of different modes, or keys, simultaneously), along with octatonic and diatonic scale fragments to construct these pieces. The compositions in the third and fourth volumes are also important because they betray the influence of Franz Liszt, particularly in terms of tone color; Bartók wrote of his desire, in these pieces, to "poetically color the piano tone." 

The final volumes (5 and 6) of the Mikrokosmos were intended as concert pieces for professional pianists. They differ from the preceding pieces in many respects: their contrapuntal texture is more dense (four parts), the melodic and harmonic material is more characteristic of Bartók's non-pedagogical works, and rhythmic structures are much more complicated and include vigorous syncopations and Bulgarian dance rhythms. 

While Bartók's intention to synthesize Bach, Beethoven, and Debussy was perhaps not fully realized, Mikrokosmos nonetheless compares well with some of Bach and Debussy's ostensibly pedagogical keyboard works. Like Bach's Inventions or Debussy's Études, for example, Mikrokosmos is not merely a work of practical value, but also a work of art with much purely musical substance. [Allmusic.com]

A simple, but evocative study by the beloved Australian composer Miriam Hyde. (Don't you think it sounds like tree branches swaying in the wind?) This piece is from the AMEB Pianoforte Studies: Third and Fourth Grades book and is listed as a Grade 3 piece. This piece is suitable for people with small hands.

I have recorded this piece at 3 different speeds to help students learn the piece accurately. Learn to play the RH quavers as evenly as possible and please take note of the long slurs, making sure to separate the notes between the slurs. Be careful not to bump the ends of the slurs (ie no accents or staccato).

Scarlatti D.Sonata in C major K 231.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in C major K. 231.
00:10 Introduction
01:12 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La Sonata in Do maggiore K. 231 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi è una Jota, una danza spagnola. Tuttavia, queso è uno di quei casi in cui il passo di danza serve a Domenico come pretesto per scrivere un pezzo estremamente raffinato: questa Sonata è scritta magnificamente, ed è piena di trucchetti. Ad esempio, il materiale tematico passa senza sosta dalla destra alla sinistra, creando così un effetto di continuità davvero interessante. Musicalmente, all'inizio della seconda parte Domenico scrive una bellissima cantilena, la quale aggiunge un tocco di intimità and un pezzo tutto sommato robusto e vivace. Presa nell'insieme, questa Sonata è molto divertente da suonare, la vera “gioia di Scarlatti”, ed è un privilegio, per me, potervela presentare.
Buon ascolto.

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 528 Bb major.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in B flat major K. 528.
00:10 Sonata
01:33 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
Coloro i quali seguono questo programma magari ricorderanno che quando introdussi diverse Sonate “giovanili” di Scarlatti, ed anche certi “Essercizi”, non feci mistero della tendenza di Domenico a scrivere un certo passo, e poi chiedere all'interprete di ripeterlo, ma a mani incrociate. Il trucco sta nel fatto che ciò che pare semplice alla mano destra diventa piuttosto scomodo alla sinistra, specialmente se lo si deve eseguire in una posizione che ricorda quella di una camicia di forza! La Sonata in Si bemolle maggiore K. 528 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi ha tutte queste caratteristiche, ma mentre negli “Essercizi” certe diavolerie tecniche erano dispiegate per far colpo, magari per abbacinare l'uditorio, qui sono messe al mero servizio d'un pezzo di musica semplice e divertente. Non ho alcun dubbio che questa Sonata sia uscita dalla penna di un Domenico Maturo, e mi garba immaginarmelo mentre siede al clavicembalo,improvvisa qualcosa di simile per un piccolo uditorio, e poi fa l'occhiolino al suo pubblico dicendogli: “Vedete? Mi riesce ancora! Certo che Le riesce, Maestro!
Buon ascolto.

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 524 F major.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in F major K. 524.
00:10 Introduction
02:49 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
Facciamo finta d'avere una meravigliosa macchina del tempo, la quale ci ha portato indietro negli anni fino a circa il 1750. Siamo a Madrid, al palazzo reale, e la Regina Maria Barbara sta dando una festa. Ad un certo punto, desidera ballare e fa chiamare Domenico: “Don Domenico – gli chiede – sareste così gentile da suonarci un Minuetto?”. In qualità di regio Maestro di Musica, Domenico non può certo dire di no, sicché si siede al clavicembalo e suona un minuetto. Gli ospiti danzano, e quando Domenico termina il suo minuetto gli chiedono di suonarne un altro, poi un altro, e così via fino a che Domenico finisce i suoi minuetti (ne ha scritti una decina, e se siete interessati su questo canale troverete un video speciale con tutti i minuetti di Domenico al link alla fine di questo episodio). Ma la Regina vul sempre ballare, sicché a Domenico non resta che improvvisare un minuetto seduta stante. Capita trovarsi nel tono di Fa maggiore, e comincia ad improvvisare, ma lui è Domenico Scarlatti, mago della musica, ed a questo punto non ne può più di fare il “jukebox” umano e suonare musica da ballo. Decide di vivacizzare la situazione: ad esempio, nel minuetto si fa la riverenza sul terzo tempo della battuta, ma a Domenico viene l'idea birichina di mettere la riverenza sul primo tempo della battuta, creando scompiglio. Gli va a genio fare il mascalzone musicale, e comincia ad infarcire la musica con variazione dopo variazione, tanto che nella seconda parte si lascia andare in un passo focoso a quattro voci, pieno d'ottave e parecchio reboante. A questo punto, ovviamente, nessuno balla più: son tutti lì a godersi lo spettacolo del vecchio virtuoso che si diverte come un matto a suonare... Ora, questa storiella è frutto della mia forse troppo florida fantasia, ma secondo me è del tutto plausibile, e specialmente se la raccontiamo assieme alla Sonata in Fa maggiore K. 524 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi. Questa Sonata, secondo me, è un “minuetto con variazioni”. E, sempre secondo me, è anche un pezzo di musica bellissimo, accattivante, ed è mio grande privilegio potervelo presentare.
Buon ascolto.

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 542 F major.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in F major K. 542-
00:10 Introduction
01:44 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La grande Sonata in Fa maggiore K. 542 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi è un pezzo che non dovrebbe funzionare, in quanto è troppo ricco di differenti idee musicali. A prima vista, questa musica assomiglia più agli scarabocchi di un pazzo che non al prodotto della mente di un grande maestro. La Sonata comincia in modo contrappuntistico, con la mano destra che canta due voci le quali, poi, passano alla sinistra mentre la destra commenta con graziose fioriture. Poi Domenico modula nel tono minore, e scrive musica del tutto differente. Poi dispiega qualche scala fulminante, e poi c'è un episodio di fanfara che produce un'esplosione di suono. Ad un occhio esperto, cotanta varietà di materiale suggerisce un pezzo sconnesso. Ma Domenico Scarlatti è un genio, e qui dimostra tutto il suo sapere riuscendo nella quasi impossibile impresa di fondere tutti questi temi, questi ritmi, questi spunti musicali in un pezzo di musica coeso. Nel frattempo, la scrittura tastieristica è meravigliosa dall'inizio alla fine, e dire che questa musica si adatti bene alla mano è un enorme eufemismo. Questa Sonata, amici, è un serio capolavoro.
Buon ascolto.
