Ignaz Moscheles, (born May 23, 1794, Prague, Bohemia, Austrian Habsburg domain [now in Czech Republic]—died March 10, 1870, Leipzig [Germany]), Czech pianist, one of the outstanding virtuosos of his era.
Moscheles studied at the Prague Conservatory and later at Vienna under Johann Georg Albrechtsberger and Antonio Salieri. In 1814, commissioned by Artaria & Co., publishers, he made the first piano arrangement of Ludwig van Beethoven’s opera Fidelio, under the composer’s supervision. After giving piano recitals in Germany and France, he settled in London in 1821. In 1829 he took part in the first London performance of the Concerto for Two Pianos by Felix Mendelssohn, who had been his pupil. He conducted the first English performance of Beethoven’s Missa Solemnis and later conducted Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony at the Philharmonic Society, of which he was a regular conductor from 1845. From 1846 he was principal professor of piano at the Leipzig Conservatory, and his reputation and skill as a teacher were important factors in the continued success of that institution.
Moscheles belonged to a conservative school of piano playing that did not lend itself to the works of Frédéric Chopin and Franz Liszt; of the younger composers of his day, he leaned more toward Mendelssohn and Robert Schumann. Nevertheless, his explorations of the gradations of tone colour influenced Liszt as well as Schumann. He was also admired for his brilliant extempore performances. His own compositions include eight piano concerti, studies, and chamber works.

Hans-Dieter Bauer perform's Reger's Caprice Fantastique in F sharp minor.  This track was recorded from an LP manufactured and distributed in 1974 by the Musical Heritage Society (MHS 1920). ===================================
Johann Baptist Joseph Maximilian Reger (March 19, 1873 - May 11, 1916) was a German composer, conductor, pianist, organist, and teacher.  During a composing life of little more than 25 years, Reger produced an enormous output, nearly always in abstract forms, although few of his compositions are well known today. Many of his works are fugues or in variation form, including what is probably his best known orchestral work, the Variations and Fugue on a Theme by Mozart (based on the opening theme of Mozart's Piano Sonata in A major, K. 331). He also wrote a large amount of music for organ, including the Fantasy and Fugue on BACH (this piece, based on the BACH motif, is considered one of the most difficult and demanding in organ literature). He was particularly attracted to the fugal form his entire life. Once he remarked: "Other people write fugues - I live inside them". He created music in almost every genre, opera and the symphony being the two exceptions.
==================================
Иоганн Баптист Иозеф Максимилиан Регер (нем. Johann Baptist Joseph Maximilian Reger 19 марта 1873 — 11 мая 1916) — немецкий композитор, дирижер, пианист, органист и педагог.
==================================

==================================
Max Reger, né le 19 mars 1873 à Brand en Bavière et mort le 11 mai 1916 à Leipzig est un compositeur, chef d'orchestre, pianiste, organiste et professeur de musique allemand.
==================================
Max Reger (ur. 19 marca 1873 w Brand, zm. 11 maja 1916 w Lipsku)  kompozytor i organista niemiecki.  W dorobku Regera czołową pozycję zajmują dzieła organowe, a także kameralne i symfoniczne. Reger pisał utwory o przeładowanej fakturze, wzorując się na twórczości organowej swojego mistrza  J.S.Bacha. Fascynacja ta wpływa na twórczość kameralną, fortepianową, a nawet orkiestrową dzieł Regera. Kompozytor ten używał instrumentów na wzór rejestrów organowych, czyli według stopnia ich siły i to przenosił także do muzyki orkiestrowej. Z form właściwych dla dawnej twórczości organowej pisał fugi, preludia, wariacje, toccaty, kanony, passacaglie, przygrywki chorałowe.

É autor também de obras para órgão, música de câmara, canções, obras para corais, um concerto para piano e orquestra, um concerto para violino e muitas peças para piano.

Egli seppe fondere insieme i metodi barocchi e classici con il nuovo linguaggio armonico e cromatico dell'epoca. Il suo stile quindi si colloca tra il tardo romanticismo e l'età contemporanea.

🎵 Erik Satie (17 May 1866 – 1 July 1925) was a French composer and pianist. Satie was an influential artist in the late 19th- and early 20th-century Parisian avant-garde. His work was a precursor to later artistic movements such as minimalism, repetitive music, and the Theatre of the Absurd, while his 1917 coinage "furniture music" would presage the development of background and ambient music.

An eccentric, Satie was introduced as a "gymnopedist" in 1887, shortly before writing his most famous works, the piano compositions Gymnopédies. Later, he also referred to himself as a "phonometrician" (meaning "someone who measures sounds"), preferring this designation to that of "musician", after having been called "a clumsy but subtle technician" in a book on contemporary French composers published in 1911.

Moscheles I.24 Studies Op 70 No 20.YT_description:
Ignaz Moscheles - Etude op. 70 n. 20
Fausto Bongelli, piano
Ignaz Moscheles, (born May 23, 1794, Prague, Bohemia, Austrian Habsburg domain [now in Czech Republic]—died March 10, 1870, Leipzig [Germany]), Czech pianist, one of the outstanding virtuosos of his era.
Moscheles studied at the Prague Conservatory and later at Vienna under Johann Georg Albrechtsberger and Antonio Salieri. In 1814, commissioned by Artaria & Co., publishers, he made the first piano arrangement of Ludwig van Beethoven’s opera Fidelio, under the composer’s supervision. After giving piano recitals in Germany and France, he settled in London in 1821. In 1829 he took part in the first London performance of the Concerto for Two Pianos by Felix Mendelssohn, who had been his pupil. He conducted the first English performance of Beethoven’s Missa Solemnis and later conducted Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony at the Philharmonic Society, of which he was a regular conductor from 1845. From 1846 he was principal professor of piano at the Leipzig Conservatory, and his reputation and skill as a teacher were important factors in the continued success of that institution.
Moscheles belonged to a conservative school of piano playing that did not lend itself to the works of Frédéric Chopin and Franz Liszt; of the younger composers of his day, he leaned more toward Mendelssohn and Robert Schumann. Nevertheless, his explorations of the gradations of tone colour influenced Liszt as well as Schumann. He was also admired for his brilliant extempore performances. His own compositions include eight piano concerti, studies, and chamber works.

【譜めくり日めくり#121】I. モシェレス／12の性格的練習曲　作品95　第1-3番(無編集)

1. 憤怒(Wrath), Allegro non troppo, a-moll 0:00
2. 和解(Reconciliation), Andante placido, F-dur 2:54
3. 矛盾(Contradiction), Vivace, Des-dur 6:08

モシェレスの作品95は、以前弾いた作品70と並ぶ大規模な練習曲集ですが、これよりもだいぶ手強い気がします。1曲目からもう仕上がる気がしないです。とりあえず最初の3曲をアップします。
この曲集も、全曲の録音が見つかりません。。。

この曲集は、「性格的」という語が付されていることにも表れている通り、各曲にモシェレス自身によってタイトルが与えられています。ですが、第3番の「矛盾」とは、曲の内容にどう反映されているのか今ひとつ不明です。

とにかく難曲揃いですが、頑張ります(T_T;;

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 539 G major.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in G major K. 539.
00:10 Introduction
02:00 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La Sonata in Sol maggiore K. 539 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi è un lavoro meraviglioso! A me pare una Sinfonia in miniatura: vi sono così tanti episodi che non è punto difficile immaginarne uno suonato dagli archi, un altro magari affidato ad un solo dell'oboe, ed un altro ancora ad un coro di legni; è una meraviglia! La Sonata è anche piena di peculiarità. Ad esempio, vi è un episodio subito dopo l'inizio in cui Domenico alterna continuamente fra modo maggiore e minore. Nella musica, questo si ottiene di solito alterando l'altezza della terza nota della scala, e qui Domenico lo fa con un bemolle. Ma il piazzamento di questo accidente a prima vista appare quasi casuale, e l'effetto che crea è quello di un totale disorientamento. Di conseguenza, questa Sonata è fra quelle che più hanno subito gl'interventi dei vari revisori: il Signor Longo, nella sua edizione del 1906, praticamente dette alle stampe una parafrasi, e perfino il Maestro Gilbert, la cui edizione solitamente uso per questo programma, ha infarcito la partitura di così tanti suggerimenti che ho dovuto rinunciare alla mia pratica usuale di non scrivere nulla in partitura, e segnarmi quali accidenti sono di Domenico e quali, invece, inseriti da Gilbert! Dopo questo passaggio, Domenico approda al tono di Si bemolle maggiore ed è a questo punto che la Sonata vera e propria comincia: una meravigliosa successione di episodi uno più straordinario dell'altro, ivi incluso un passo a scale doppie la cui bellezza è commovente.
Buon ascolto.

"Dear friends, good day.
Today we will approach Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in c minor K.40, a work which opens a little window over a very important facet of his output, that is to say music which was inspired by dance. Part A.Spiegel im Spiegel arr. Chan.YT_description:
Spiegel im Spiegel ('mirror in the mirror') is a composition by Estonian composer Arvo Pärt (1935 - ). The piece was written in 1978, just before his departure from Estonia. Perhaps this was meant as a melancholic goodbye to his country? 

A special thank you to TwoSet Violin for introducing me to the piece! I am usually not a fan of modern classical music. This piece however is something special. The piece symbolises an infinity mirror. The simple triads, together with an ascending and descending single note melody reflecting back and forth create such a tranquil calmness of the mind. I must say I am quite struck by its shameless simplicity. In such a chaotic year of 2020, we need this sort of meditative music more than ever. 

This piece is originally written for violin and piano, but I arranged a solo piano version. I recorded this on my beloved Estonia L210, which I find quite fitting for a modern Estonian composition.

Sheet music: https://app.box.com/s/k8dd3h0kq4gselbaccowg4rpxhcq7odp

Hensel F.Andante cantabile in Db major.YT_description:
Susan Jane Matthews, piano
Recorded March 29, 2020

Fanny Hensel (1805-1847) was a German pianist and composer of tremendous musical talent and skill like her famous younger brother, Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy (1809-1847).  While Felix’s works reached international audiences, Fanny’s were heard in Sonntagsmusiken (Sunday musicales) at the Hensel home in Berlin.  Andante cantabile, composed in 1847, commences with a singing style similar to her brother’s, though then proceeds on a daring journey through distant keys that make this song uniquely expressive of her spirit.  This work was published in 1986, among a selection of previously unpublished pieces made by Fanny Hensel’s great-granddaughter Fanny Kistner-Hensel.

Ignaz Moscheles - Etude op.70 n.6
Fausto Bongelli, piano
Ignaz Moscheles, (born May 23, 1794, Prague, Bohemia, Austrian Habsburg domain [now in Czech Republic]—died March 10, 1870, Leipzig [Germany]), Czech pianist, one of the outstanding virtuosos of his era.
Moscheles studied at the Prague Conservatory and later at Vienna under Johann Georg Albrechtsberger and Antonio Salieri. In 1814, commissioned by Artaria & Co., publishers, he made the first piano arrangement of Ludwig van Beethoven’s opera Fidelio, under the composer’s supervision. After giving piano recitals in Germany and France, he settled in London in 1821. In 1829 he took part in the first London performance of the Concerto for Two Pianos by Felix Mendelssohn, who had been his pupil. He conducted the first English performance of Beethoven’s Missa Solemnis and later conducted Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony at the Philharmonic Society, of which he was a regular conductor from 1845. From 1846 he was principal professor of piano at the Leipzig Conservatory, and his reputation and skill as a teacher were important factors in the continued success of that institution.
Moscheles belonged to a conservative school of piano playing that did not lend itself to the works of Frédéric Chopin and Franz Liszt; of the younger composers of his day, he leaned more toward Mendelssohn and Robert Schumann. Nevertheless, his explorations of the gradations of tone colour influenced Liszt as well as Schumann. He was also admired for his brilliant extempore performances. His own compositions include eight piano concerti, studies, and chamber works.

Born in Valencia (Spain) in 1988, is regarded by critics and public alike as one of the most interesting young pianists of the Spanish new generation. Winner of more than 20 national and international piano awards.
 He studied in Valencia, with Ricardo Roca and Francisco Baró, and in Paris with Denis Pascal (CNSMP teacher, pupil of Georgy Sebok). Has performed in masterclasses with such distinguished musicians as Alicia de Larrocha, Jacques Rouvier, Michel Beroff, Dimitri Bashkirov, Lazar Berman, Sergio Perticaroli, Jerome Rose, Akiko Ebi, Boris Petrushansky, Sergei Dorensky, Alexander Lonquich, Joaquin Soriano, Rudolf Buchbinder and others. In 2010 he was admitted to the prestigious Italian Academy “Incontri col Maestro” in Imola (where he continue his studies). Becoming the first Spanish be accepted in this institution, where he focussed his studies on the Russian school under the guidance of the famed Leonid Margarius (pupil of Regina Horowitz, who was the sister of pianist Vladimir Horowitz). 
 He has performed in different cities of Spain, France, Italy, Austria and Germany. He has been invited in international festivals such as the "Pianale", "Classic Pyrenees," "Humanitarian" or "Musicians of the world" (Eutherpe Foundation). Pavel Kolesnikov was born in Novosibirsk on 25.02.1989 in the family of scientists. He began to study piano and violin at age six. After study with prof. Moscheles I.Etude in Ab major No 9 from.YT_description:
Ignaz Moscheles - Etude op.70 n.9
Fausto Bongelli, piano
Ignaz Moscheles, (born May 23, 1794, Prague, Bohemia, Austrian Habsburg domain [now in Czech Republic]—died March 10, 1870, Leipzig [Germany]), Czech pianist, one of the outstanding virtuosos of his era.
Moscheles studied at the Prague Conservatory and later at Vienna under Johann Georg Albrechtsberger and Antonio Salieri. In 1814, commissioned by Artaria & Co., publishers, he made the first piano arrangement of Ludwig van Beethoven’s opera Fidelio, under the composer’s supervision. After giving piano recitals in Germany and France, he settled in London in 1821. In 1829 he took part in the first London performance of the Concerto for Two Pianos by Felix Mendelssohn, who had been his pupil. He conducted the first English performance of Beethoven’s Missa Solemnis and later conducted Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony at the Philharmonic Society, of which he was a regular conductor from 1845. From 1846 he was principal professor of piano at the Leipzig Conservatory, and his reputation and skill as a teacher were important factors in the continued success of that institution.
Moscheles belonged to a conservative school of piano playing that did not lend itself to the works of Frédéric Chopin and Franz Liszt; of the younger composers of his day, he leaned more toward Mendelssohn and Robert Schumann. Nevertheless, his explorations of the gradations of tone colour influenced Liszt as well as Schumann. He was also admired for his brilliant extempore performances. His own compositions include eight piano concerti, studies, and chamber works.

Scarlatti D.Sonata in A major K. 279.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in A major K. 279
00:10 Introduction
01:29 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La prima volta che vidi la musica della Sonata in La maggiore K. 279 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi, non potevo credere ai miei occhi. Per farla semplice, questo è uno dei pezzi di musica più belli che io abbia mai ascoltato! La Sonata reca l'indicazione di tempo “Andante”, e comincia con un bellissimo canto aperto, riminiscenza d'una ninnananna. Curiosamente, questo canto è anche molto simmetrico, tanto da far pensare ad una filastrocca. Ma dopo aver esposto questo tema semplice, Domenico comincia ad apportare piccole variazioni, a modulare (si spingerà piuttosto lontano dal tono d'impianto di La maggiore), e di punto in bianco ci rendiamo conto d'essere nel bel mezzo d'un capolavoro. Questo lavoro di sviluppo ed espansione raggiunge il suo apice nella seconda parte, ove si trova un espisodio di acceso lirismo nel quale possiamo toccare con mano l'immensa eredità operistica della quale Domenico era ereditario. Dissipato il dramma, la musica torna all'atmosfera serena degli esordi, e si chiude in un clima di pacata bonomia. Questo, amici, è un capolavoro.
Buon ascolto.

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 521 G major.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in G major K. 521.
00:10 Introduction
01:59 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
L'aggettivo “spettacolare”, quando usato accanto alla musica di Domenico Scarlatti, tende a far pensare a virtuosismi al calor bianco, grandi salti, lunghi passi a mani incrociate, ottave doppie e mercanzia del genere. A mio parere, però, possiamo benissimo usarlo in riferimento alle straordinarie doti inventive e musicali di questo individuo. La Sonata in Sol maggiore K. 521 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi non è punto spettacolare sotto il profilo tecnico, ma lo è sotto quello musicale. Questa è una di quelle Sonate che si rivelano poco a poco: comincia con un tema pastorale su di un ritmo di siciliano, tutto molto innocente. Poi Domenico modula nel tono di Fa maggiore e vi è un momento di stasi: Domenico pare indeciso sul da farsi. Di punto in bianco l'ornamentazione si fa più densa, raggiungiamo il tono di Re maggiore e, finalmente, la Sonata si rivela per quello che è: un gioioso fandango festaiolo! A questo punto Domenico non ha più remore, ed il resto della Sonata è una esplosione di gioia. In verità, all'inizio della seconda parte vi è un momento più riflessivo ma questo è quasi filosofico: è come se Domenico ci ammonisse dicendo “vedete? Potete anche essere tristi, e quindi divertitevi finché potete”. È un pezzo che a me pare davvero molto bello, ed è mio privilegio potervelo presentare.
Buon ascolto.

Scarlatti D.Capriccio in G major K 63.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in G major K. 63 "Capriccio".
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La Sonata in Sol maggiore K. 63 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo fra poco reca il sottotitolo "Capriccio". Storicamente, i capricci erano brevi pezzi brillanti, scritti per esaltare la virtuosità di un dato esecutore, ma Domenico si discosta dalla moda predominante, qui. La Sonata è brillante, eccome, non certo virtuosistica come tante sue consorelle ma molto divertente e, soprattutto, umoristica. Sembrerebbe che per Domenico il termine "Capriccio" sia sinonimo di "Scherzo". Infatti il Nostro dissemina nella sua Sonata una serie di piccole ma piccanti dissonanze, le quali non hanno altra funzione se non quella di apparire come errori! Ebbene, errori non lo sono, ma divertenti assai si!
Buon ascolto.
Scarlatti D.Capriccio in G major K 63.YT_title: SCARLATTI / ALL SONATAS #109: Sonata in G major K. 63 "Capriccio"

Moscheles I.Studie in A minor No 5 from.YT_description:
Ignaz Moscheles - Etude op. 70 n. 5
Fausto Bongelli, piano
Ignaz Moscheles, (born May 23, 1794, Prague, Bohemia, Austrian Habsburg domain [now in Czech Republic]—died March 10, 1870, Leipzig [Germany]), Czech pianist, one of the outstanding virtuosos of his era.
Moscheles studied at the Prague Conservatory and later at Vienna under Johann Georg Albrechtsberger and Antonio Salieri. In 1814, commissioned by Artaria & Co., publishers, he made the first piano arrangement of Ludwig van Beethoven’s opera Fidelio, under the composer’s supervision. After giving piano recitals in Germany and France, he settled in London in 1821. In 1829 he took part in the first London performance of the Concerto for Two Pianos by Felix Mendelssohn, who had been his pupil. He conducted the first English performance of Beethoven’s Missa Solemnis and later conducted Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony at the Philharmonic Society, of which he was a regular conductor from 1845. From 1846 he was principal professor of piano at the Leipzig Conservatory, and his reputation and skill as a teacher were important factors in the continued success of that institution.
Moscheles belonged to a conservative school of piano playing that did not lend itself to the works of Frédéric Chopin and Franz Liszt; of the younger composers of his day, he leaned more toward Mendelssohn and Robert Schumann. Nevertheless, his explorations of the gradations of tone colour influenced Liszt as well as Schumann. He was also admired for his brilliant extempore performances. His own compositions include eight piano concerti, studies, and chamber works.

This one is a very easy piece that took me 10 minutes to learn the notes and 45 to get it up to speed and glitchless. Maybe I'm already playing it too fast, but hey, this is a very small happy donkey with a very round belly bopping left and right.
I know I could work on a more precise articulation, and my fingers, especially thumb, aren't hovering above the keys where they should, but I am tired now, and I needed some easy fun-no-work-piece, because Chopin 34.2 is killing me.
Sometimes it is important to just play and have fun and not take everything seriously.

Bach@Home; 
Magdalena Baczewska, piano

River Gods, Cascades, and Brooks, in Two Themes

Ravel wrote Jeux d’eau in 1901, adding this inscription: “Dieu fluvial riant de l'eau qui le chatouille [River god laughing as the water tickles him …”]. The composer himself said that the piece was “inspired by the noise of water and by the musical sounds which make one hear the sprays of water, the cascades, and the brooks.”  Ravel chose to set the piece in a traditional sonata form, with two themes. 
In this episode of Bach@Home, pianist Magdalena Baczewska performs and discusses Ravel’s “pianistic novelty.”

Raff J.Romance Op 2.YT_description:
Despite its low opus number, this piece is actually a late work by the Swiss composer Joachim Raff (1822-82), written in 1875, and reusing an opus number first used for a different set of pieces written in 1842. This was the strange result of Raff returning to the publisher Breitkopf & Härtel after a long gap.   The Romance is marked Adagio quasi andante, but that reflects the overall pace and mood of the piece - the crotchet metronome marking is actually 116, which looks strange at first sight.  For more information on this piece and on Raff and his work, visit tinyurl.com/yeug97kz
Note that this piece was on the 2012-2014 Trinity Guildhall Piano Grade 6 syllabus - an excellent choice!

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 507 Eb major.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in E flat major K. 507.
00:10 Introduction
02:16 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La storia dell'Arte ci insegna che quasi sempre i grandi maestri hanno avuto anche grandi allievi. Leondardo da Vinci e Pico della Mirandola, nella musica Franz Joseph Haydn con Mozart e Beethoven (perché lui era speciale), Carl Czerny con Franz Liszt, ed il nostro beneamato Domenico ebbe a lezione Padre Antonio Soler, probabilmente il più importante dei suoi allievi. Se provassimo ad immaginare un grande maestro di musica, come senza dubbio era Domenico, il quale volesse impartire ad un allievo particolarmente dotato tutto il suo sapere racchiuso nei confini di un singolo pezzo di musica, probabilmente il frutto della nostra fantasia ci porterebbe molto vicini alla meravigliosa Sonata in Mi bemolle maggiore K. 507 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi. La Sonata reca l'indicazione di “Andantino cantabile”, ed ha la forma di una lunga aria d'opera. Nell'arco di questo pezzo, Domenico ne combina di tutti i colori e fa cose che hanno dell'incredibile. Prima di tutto con l'armonia: modula in continuazione, si allontana tantissimo dal tono d'impianto di Mi bemolle, e saltabecca fra modo maggiore e minore creando un ipnotico gioco di luci e di ombre. Tecnicamente, la Sonata è scritta in modo anch'esse incredibile; ci sono infiniti abbellimenti, c'è la polifonia, c'è ovviamente lo stile cantabile, ma quel che colpisce di più è la sensazione che la Sonata nel suo intero genera nell'ascoltatore: una sensazione di profonda umanità. Questo è un capolavoro sotto ogni punto di vista, e mi piace immaginare il nostro Domenico che lo dà al suo allievo prediletto Antonio Soler mentre, col sorriso sulle labbra, gli dice “vai a studiare, ragazzo mio. Hai tanto da imparare”.
Buon ascolto.
Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 507 Eb major.YT_title: SCARLATTI / ALL SONATAS #381: Sonata in E flat major K. 507

In my humble opinion, the finest arrangement of the popular "Canon in D" is by the great Russian composer Sergei Lyapunov (1859-1924). Thus, in this version I have taken Lyapunov's original of 57 measures, reduced it to 35 measures, and made some slight modifications here and there. "Herbert Jeffrey "Herbie" Hancock (born April 12, 1940) is an American pianist, keyboardist, bandleader and composer.[1] As part of Miles Davis's Second Great Quintet, Hancock helped to redefine the role of a jazz rhythm section and was one of the primary architects of the "post-bop" sound. He was one of the first jazz musicians to embrace music synthesizers and funk music (characterized by syncopated drum beats). Hancock's music is often melodic and accessible; he has had many songs "cross over" and achieved success among pop audiences. His music embraces elements of funk and soul while adopting freer stylistic elements from jazz. In his jazz improvisation, he possesses a unique creative blend of jazz, blues, and modern classical music, with harmonic stylings much like the styles of Claude Debussy and Maurice Ravel.
Hancock's best-known solo works include "Cantaloupe Island", "Watermelon Man" (later performed by dozens of musicians, including bandleader Mongo Santamaría), "Maiden Voyage", "Chameleon", and the singles "I Thought It Was You" and "Rockit". His 2007 tribute album River: The Joni Letters won the 2008 Grammy Award for Album of the Year, only the second jazz album ever to win the award, after Getz/Gilberto in 1965.
Hancock practices Nichiren Buddhism and is a member of the Buddhist association Sōka Gakkai International.[2][3][4] As part of Hancock's spiritual practice, he recites the Buddhist chant Nam Myoho Renge Kyo each day.[5] In 2013, Hancock's dialogue with Wayne Shorter and Daisaku Ikeda on jazz, Buddhism and life was published in Japanese.
On July 22, 2011 at a ceremony in Paris, Hancock was named UNESCO Goodwill Ambassador for the promotion of Intercultural Dialogue. In 2013 Hancock joined the University of California, Los Angeles faculty as a professor in the UCLA music department where he will teach jazz music.[6]
Hancock is the 2014 Charles Eliot Norton Professor of Poetry at Harvard University. Holders of the chair deliver a series of six lectures on poetry, "The Norton Lectures", poetry being "interpreted in the broadest sense, including all poetic expression in language, music, or fine arts." Previous Norton lecturers include musicians Leonard Bernstein, Igor Stravinsky and John Cage. Hancock's theme is "The Ethics of Jazz."[7]"

These Six Preludes (1954) offer a great variety of style within 20th Century music.

John Psathas, ONZM (b.1966) is a New Zealand composer, son of Greek immigrant parents. He has not only achieved a level of international success as a composer unprecedented in New Zealand history, he is also now widely considered one of the most important living composers of the Greek diaspora.

Jettatura (1999), the “evil eye”, is the ancient belief that the gaze of strangers casts unwanted magic into the lives of the innocent. The belief is that a person can harm you by looking at you enviously and praising you. When John Psathas spent time in Greece in the summer of 1998, he experienced a remarkable sequence of unfortunate events. Upon being tested by the local specialist in these matters, it was discovered that he had indeed fallen under the influence of the “evil eye”.

Characteristic elements of the piece are the use of Greek folk rhythms and modes, the improvisational feel of jazz music and the sustained repetitive textures of minimalism. A great test for advanced pianists, Jettatura is an uncomplicated moto perpetuo, and another example of Psathas’s gift for creating high-energy, compelling works. Requiring heavy and impassioned fingering, Jettatura is shot through with defiance and aggression. The left hand hammers a stream of ostinatos while the right hand flies almost incautiously over the keys, stretching to the piano’s upper register.

Whitehead G.Arapatiki.YT_description:
GILLIAN WHITEHEAD: Arapatiki

Pianist Liam Furey delivers an impressive performance of Gillian Whitehead’s ‘Arapatiki’ in this Resound film from SMP Ensemble’s concert ‘Inside-Out’.  

Gillian writes, “Arapatiki translates as 'the way of the flounder', and is the ancient name of the sand flats in front of my house at Harwood, near Dunedin. The piece has something to do with the advance and retreat of the tide across the flats, where many species of sea and water birds spend much of the day - an ever-varying water-scape. The opening idea is based on the song of the korimako or bellbird.”

The work was commissioned by Stephen De Pledge for his Landscape Preludes series, and received its first performance at Wigmore Hall in 2004. 

Audio recorded by Phil Brownlee.

Film funded by NZ On Air.

I can find little information on Sandré, except that he was born in Paris, and taught harmony at the Nancy Conservatory, where one of his pupils was the 17 year old Florent Schmitt.  At some time in the 1890s he left Nancy for Brussels, and taught at the conservatory there.  As well as composing, he was an arranger - for example, he arranged Rubinstein's popular 4th piano concerto for four hands -  and in 1908 he translated into French Johann Christian Lobe's 1869 German musical primer 'Katechismus der Musik' (A Musical Catechism).

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 522 G major.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in G major K. 522.
00:10 Introduction
02:27 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
Mi accorgo ora che prima di cominciare questo progetto avrei fatto bene a prendere qualche lezione di vocabolario: ogni giorno son qui a raccontarvi quanto siano meravigliose queste Sonate, una dopo l'altra, e ormai sono a corto di aggettivi! Oggi non fa eccezione: la Sonata in Sol maggiore K. 522 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo fra poco è, almeno nella mia opinione, un capolavoro. Si tratta di un lavoro piuttosto contrappuntistico, che comincia come un canone (vale a dire con le due mani che eseguono le stesse note, ma a tempi e ad intervalli diversi: si rincorrono su e giù per la tastiera come il gatto col topo). C'è poi un episodio più lirico, molto bello, ma la “colonna portante” del pezzo è una figura particolare che si presenta solo alla mano sinistra. Detta figura è fatta da un arpeggio che sale per due ottave e poi, sull'ultima nota, compie un salto di ottava. Detta così pare roba da poco, ma in pratica suona come il ruggito di un leone! Una cosa interessantissima, la quale aggiunge una bella pennellata di colore ad un pezzo di musica già fantastico. Voglio spendere una parola a proposito della popolarità di questa Sonata. Anche qui su Youtube si trovano pochissime letture di questo bel pezzo, ed a me pare un gran peccato. So che diversi insegnanti di pianoforte seguono questo programma, ed a me la Sonata in Sol maggiore pare un punto d'ingresso ideale nell'universo scarlattiano: non è molto difficile tecnicamente, ma ha in corpo tanti elementi dello stile di questo grande Maestro. Sicché, vi chiedo d'ascoltarla e, se vi piace, assegnatela ai vostri studenti. Mi farebbe immenso piacere se più pianisti suonassero questa bella musica. Dal mio canto, fra poco tornerò a fare il mio lavoro, ossia il concertista di pianoforte. Sono certissimo che questa Sonata il Sol maggiore sarà senz'altro nei programmi dei miei prossimi recital.
Buon ascolto.

Scarlatti D.Sonata - K 538 G major.YT_description:
Sandro Ivo Bartoli plays Domenico Scarlatti's Sonata in G major K. 538.
00:10 Introduction
01:37 Sonata
Sandro dice:
Cari amici buongiorno,
La Sonata in Sol maggiore K. 538 di Domenico Scarlatti che presenteremo oggi reca l'indicazione di “Allegretto”, ed è un “tempo di ballo” per eccellenza. Se voleste, potreste ballare il fandango su questa Sonata. La musica è estremamente idiomatica: di colpo, ci troviamo catapultati nella Spagna del Settecento, magari in un piccolo villaggio ove è in corso una festa: un'orchestrina accompagna un gruppo di danzatori con un motivo piuttoso allegro, il quale però di tanto in tanto si tinge di quella particolare malinconia che è propria dei popoli mediterranei. Questa, comunque, non è mera musica da ballo bensì una Sonata matura dalla penna di Domenico il quale, evidentemente, si diverte un mondo a suonare il piccolo fandango. La musica è scritta molto bene, ed è atipicamente densa: entrambe le mani, infatti, portano aavanti due voci ciascuna, e questo crea delle interessanti possibilità strumentali. Vi è l'imitazione degli srumenti popolari, vi sono grandi gesta quasi coreografiche, e via discorrendo. Alla fine, in modo del tutto originale, Domenico chiude la Sonata con un Sol grave in tempo di levare: quasi volesse inchinarsi al suo pubblico mormorando “alla prossima”...
Buon ascolto.

Emmanuel Oriol  ( Ne Tirez pas sur le pianiste!) Don't shoot the Pianist!

This Chaplinesque character will undoubtedly make  Don't shoot the Pianist a popular choice. It is written  in a lively ragtime style and a with that comes as great excitement of a leaping left hand.
Left hand must jump to its notes unsupervised, since the focus of attention is uppermost on the nimble and snappy melody.

It is very important to practice separate hands at first. Left hand needs to develop an independent physical memory for the bass line notes and chords.
The bass notes should be played with warmth and length, with a lightening of the hand for the chords.
The right hand should be witty and fluent, There are variety of articulation involved. 
Tempo must be carefully picked, to achieve great control , accuracy and a subtlety of shape .

Don't shoot the pianist will suit an adventurous and brave player.

Due for release on 7 October on Deutsche Grammophon, the highly personal double album reflects Ólafsson’s musical DNA, from childhood memories growing up in Iceland to his international career and contemporary inspirations. Recorded on both upright and grand pianos, the album captures two distinct sound worlds with works by Bach, Mozart, Schumann, Brahms and Bartók, alongside Icelandic and Hungarian folk songs, a world premiere by Thomas Adès, transcriptions by Ólafsson himself, and interconnecting pieces composed by his hero, 96 year-old Hungarian composer and pianist György Kurtág. Moscheles I.Studie No 14 from Studien Op.YT_description:
I. Moscheles Etude op.70 n.14
Fausto Bongelli, piano
Ignaz Moscheles, (born May 23, 1794, Prague, Bohemia, Austrian Habsburg domain [now in Czech Republic]—died March 10, 1870, Leipzig [Germany]), Czech pianist, one of the outstanding virtuosos of his era.
Moscheles studied at the Prague Conservatory and later at Vienna under Johann Georg Albrechtsberger and Antonio Salieri. In 1814, commissioned by Artaria & Co., publishers, he made the first piano arrangement of Ludwig van Beethoven’s opera Fidelio, under the composer’s supervision. After giving piano recitals in Germany and France, he settled in London in 1821. In 1829 he took part in the first London performance of the Concerto for Two Pianos by Felix Mendelssohn, who had been his pupil. He conducted the first English performance of Beethoven’s Missa Solemnis and later conducted Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony at the Philharmonic Society, of which he was a regular conductor from 1845. From 1846 he was principal professor of piano at the Leipzig Conservatory, and his reputation and skill as a teacher were important factors in the continued success of that institution.
Moscheles belonged to a conservative school of piano playing that did not lend itself to the works of Frédéric Chopin and Franz Liszt; of the younger composers of his day, he leaned more toward Mendelssohn and Robert Schumann. Nevertheless, his explorations of the gradations of tone colour influenced Liszt as well as Schumann. He was also admired for his brilliant extempore performances. His own compositions include eight piano concerti, studies, and chamber works.

▸https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six_moments_musicaux_(Rachmaninoff)
Six moments musicaux (French for "Six Musical Moments), Op. 16, is a set of solo piano pieces composed by the Russian composer Sergei Rachmaninoff 1896. Each Moment musical reproduces a musical form characteristic of a previous musical era. The forms that appear in Rachmaninoff's incarnation are the nocturne, song without words, barcarolle, virtuoso étude, and theme and variations.
The individual pieces have been described as "true concert works, being best served on a stage and with a concert grand." Although composed as part of a set, each piece stands on its own as a concert solo with individual themes and moods. The pieces span a variety of themes ranging from the somber funeral march of number three to the majestic canon of number six, the Moments musicaux are both Rachmaninoff's return to and revolution of solo piano composition. 
In an interview in 1941, Rachmaninoff said, "What I try to do, when writing down my music, is to make it say simply and directly that which is in my heart when I am composing." Even though Moments musicaux were written because he was short of money, the pieces summarize his knowledge of piano composition up to that point. Andantino opens the set with a long, reflective melody that develops into a rapid climax. The second piece, Allegretto, is the first of the few in the set that reveal his mastery of piano technique. Andante cantabile is a contrast to its two surrounding pieces, explicitly named "funeral march" and "lament." Presto draws inspiration from several sources, including the Preludes of Frédéric Chopin, to synthesize an explosion of melodic intensity. The fifth, Adagio sostenuto is a respite in barcarolle form, before the finale Maestoso, which closes the set in a thick three-part texture. In six musical moments, Rachmaninoff illustrates completely, "that which is in my heart."
(Wikipedia)

His recital consisted of only his works for piano.  Muczynski studied piano with Walter Knupfer and composition with Alexander Tcherepnin at DePaul University  in Chicago. Ignaz Moscheles - Etude op.70 n. 8
Fausto Bongelli, piano
Ignaz Moscheles, (born May 23, 1794, Prague, Bohemia, Austrian Habsburg domain [now in Czech Republic]—died March 10, 1870, Leipzig [Germany]), Czech pianist, one of the outstanding virtuosos of his era.
Moscheles studied at the Prague Conservatory and later at Vienna under Johann Georg Albrechtsberger and Antonio Salieri. In 1814, commissioned by Artaria & Co., publishers, he made the first piano arrangement of Ludwig van Beethoven’s opera Fidelio, under the composer’s supervision. After giving piano recitals in Germany and France, he settled in London in 1821. In 1829 he took part in the first London performance of the Concerto for Two Pianos by Felix Mendelssohn, who had been his pupil. He conducted the first English performance of Beethoven’s Missa Solemnis and later conducted Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony at the Philharmonic Society, of which he was a regular conductor from 1845. From 1846 he was principal professor of piano at the Leipzig Conservatory, and his reputation and skill as a teacher were important factors in the continued success of that institution.
Moscheles belonged to a conservative school of piano playing that did not lend itself to the works of Frédéric Chopin and Franz Liszt; of the younger composers of his day, he leaned more toward Mendelssohn and Robert Schumann. Nevertheless, his explorations of the gradations of tone colour influenced Liszt as well as Schumann. He was also admired for his brilliant extempore performances. His own compositions include eight piano concerti, studies, and chamber works.
